# Design system

The portfolio has a light and a dark theme. Every color, font, radius, shadow and motion value lives in
[`src/styles/tokens.css`](../src/styles/tokens.css) as a Tailwind v4 `@theme` token, written in OKLCH; each color is
`light-dark(light, dark)`, so the page follows the reader's system and the header's theme button pins one by setting
`<html data-theme>` (remembered in `localStorage` and applied before the first paint by the script in
`layouts/Page.astro`). `--color-*: initial` removes Tailwind's default palette, so a class such as `text-blue-500` does
not compile and components can only use the tokens below. [`DESIGN.md`](../DESIGN.md) explains where the look comes
from.

## Brand

The interface is monochrome: ink on paper in the light theme, paper on ink in the dark one. Color lives in the layers:
the tiles behind the illustrations, the illustrations themselves and the charts. One cobalt marks what must stand out
without shouting.

| Role                | Token               | Light     | Dark      |
|---------------------|---------------------|-----------|-----------|
| Ink (text, actions) | `fg` = `primary`    | `#141619` | `#F5F5F5` |
| Paper (page)        | `bg` = `on-primary` | `#FBFCFD` | `#0D0D0D` |
| Cobalt              | `accent`            | `#1745C2` | `#9DBDFF` |
| Focus               | `ring`              | `#3266E4` | `#77A2FC` |

The previous identity, a teal on near-black with a serif display face, read as heavy and hard to scan; the redesign of
November 2026 moved the color out of the interface and into the images.

## Semantic tokens

| Token                          | Use                                                            | On `bg`, light / dark |
|--------------------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------|-----------------------|
| `bg`                           | Page background, also `theme-color`                            | —                     |
| `surface`                      | Panels, the skill cards, raised sections                       | —                     |
| `surface-raised`               | Chips, quiet buttons, hovers                                   | —                     |
| `border`                       | Decorative dividers between rows                               | decorative only       |
| `border-strong`                | Input borders and controls that must be visible                | 3.8:1 / 4.2:1         |
| `fg`                           | Headings and body text                                         | 17.6:1 / 17.8:1       |
| `fg-muted`                     | Summaries, briefs, descriptions                                | 10.1:1 / 11.9:1       |
| `fg-subtle`                    | Captions, dates, eyebrows                                      | 8.6:1 / 9.4:1         |
| `primary`                      | Primary buttons and active pills (the ink)                     | 17.6:1 / 17.8:1       |
| `on-primary`                   | Text on `primary`                                              | 17.6:1 / 17.8:1       |
| `accent`                       | The current menu entry's dot, the first chart series           | 7.6:1 / 10.3:1        |
| `ring`                         | Focus outline                                                  | 4.9:1 / 7.7:1         |
| `success`, `warning`, `danger` | Status text and icons                                          | ≥ 7:1                 |
| `tile-*`                       | The layer behind each illustration (eight hues)                | —                     |
| `ink`, `paper`                 | Text on the fixed colors of the UN goal badges                 | —                     |
| `whatsapp`, `on-whatsapp`      | WhatsApp button, the only brand color from outside the palette | —                     |

`pnpm check:contrast` ([`scripts/check-contrast.mjs`](../scripts/check-contrast.mjs)) converts every token from OKLCH
to sRGB, takes each half of `light-dark()` in turn and checks these minimums in both themes; the build pipeline fails
when one drops below them:

| Pair                                                           | Minimum           |
|----------------------------------------------------------------|-------------------|
| `fg`, `fg-muted`, `fg-subtle`, `primary` on every surface      | 7:1 (AAA)         |
| `fg`, `fg-muted` on every `tile-*`                             | 7:1 (AAA)         |
| `accent`, `danger`, `success`, `warning` on `bg` and `surface` | 7:1 (AAA)         |
| `on-primary` on `primary` and `primary-hover`                  | 7:1 (AAA)         |
| `border-strong` and `ring` on every surface                    | 3:1 (WCAG 1.4.11) |
| `on-whatsapp` on `whatsapp`                                    | 3:1               |
| `viz-*` on `bg` and `surface`                                  | 3:1               |
| `level-*` on `bg` and `surface`                                | 2:1               |
| `bg` on `level-2` to `level-4`, `fg` on `level-1`              | 4.5:1             |
| `paper` or `ink` on each `sdg-*`                               | 4.5:1             |

Every text color reaches AAA on the surfaces it sits on, in both themes. The one exception is the number inside an
SDG badge: the badges keep the UN's own colors, on which neither light nor dark ink reaches 7:1, so the number stays at
AA in a fixed `paper` or `ink` and the goal's name, written beside the badge in `fg-muted` (or read out to screen
readers where the badge is compact), carries the same meaning.

## Illustrations

The projects, the hero, the skills and every page beyond the projects are illustrated with one family of drawings:
soft hardware seen from above, built from rounded plates with a darker side for thickness, a sheen, a bevel and a
blurred contact shadow, plus lenses, lights, keys, screens and cables. `scripts/render-illustrations.mjs` draws them
from `scripts/illustrations` (`kit.mjs` is the drawing kit, `scenes.mjs` one object per project, `hero.mjs` the hero's
board, `lab.mjs` the objects of the skill groups that borrow none from a project, `pages.mjs` one object per service,
reason to hire, job, program and GitHub organization) into `public/illustrations` as static SVG, and writes
`src/content/shared/project-art.ts` and `page-art.ts`, the maps the components read. In `pages.mjs` a job is a badge,
a program a book with what it led to on top, an organization a cabinet (with a padlock when its code is private), and
a flat glyph (`GLYPHS`) pressed into a face tells the objects of one kind apart. That map includes `HERO_SPOTS`, the box
each device of the hero's board fills (in `hero.mjs`,
`DEVICES`), which `HeroSection` covers with a link to the device's project; the labels' copy is `hero.board` in each
language, and a test keeps each label's name equal to its project's. Run `pnpm illustrations` after changing a scene and
commit what it writes; `--sheet` also writes a
contact sheet of every drawing on its tile in both themes.

The drawings have transparent backgrounds: the page lays each one on its `tile-*`, so the same file works in both
themes. Their colors are fixed and chosen to read on both a pastel and a deep tile; line work uses a mid grey rather
than graphite for that reason. They are loaded as images, so they add nothing to the JavaScript, and a light inside
one may pulse three times or a dial sweep once; nothing loops.

## Data visualization

The journey section draws charts, so it has its own tokens. They sit in a `@theme static` block at the end of
`tokens.css`, because the charts read them through inline `var(--color-…)` values that Tailwind cannot see, and a
plain `@theme` would drop them from the CSS. Every palette was checked with the dataviz palette validator for
color-vision deficiencies as well as contrast; the line hues sit at a lightness that reads on both themes.

**Lines** (`viz-*`): one categorical hue per career line of the journey map, always in this order so that the
neighboring lanes keep the most distinct pairs. The worst adjacent pair stays apart under protanopia, deuteranopia and
tritanopia (ΔE 8.4). Colors never carry meaning alone: every lane has a text label and every station a name.

| Token           | Line                   | Hex       | On `surface` |
|-----------------|------------------------|-----------|--------------|
| `viz-education` | Education              | `#3987E5` | 5.0:1        |
| `viz-web`       | Web & full-stack       | `#D95926` | 4.7:1        |
| `viz-backend`   | Backend & integrations | `#1A9E70` | 5.4:1        |
| `viz-crm`       | CRM & automation       | `#C98500` | 6.0:1        |
| `viz-data`      | Data & BI              | `#D55181` | 4.6:1        |
| `viz-devops`    | DevOps & cloud         | `#008300` | 3.7:1        |
| `viz-security`  | Security               | `#9085E9` | 5.9:1        |

**Levels** (`level-1` … `level-4`): an ordinal cobalt ramp for the capability heatmap and the rings of the focus
radar, from the step closest to the page to the one that stands out most: light to dark in the light theme, dark to
light in the dark one. Level 0 is the empty `surface`. Numbers drawn on levels 2–4 use `bg`; on level 1 they use `fg`.

**Sustainable Development Goals** (`sdg-*`): the official UN colors of goals 2, 4, 8, 9, 11, 13 and 16, kept exact
because they are recognizable. Their number badges use `paper` on goals 4, 8, 13 and 16 and `ink` on goals 2, 9 and 11,
whichever clears 4.5:1, in either theme.

The radar's four quadrants are not colored: four hues on one chart failed the all-pairs color-vision check, so
quadrants are told apart by position and labels, and only the ring (focus level) is colored.

## Typography

| Token          | Font                | Use                                                  |
|----------------|---------------------|------------------------------------------------------|
| `font-display` | DM Serif Text 400   | `h1`–`h3`; hierarchy comes from size, never bold     |
| `font-sans`    | IBM Plex Sans 400/600 | Body text and UI                                   |
| `font-mono`    | Source Code Pro 400 | Tech chips, dates, eyebrows, code, the ASCII art     |

| Token          | Size                                                                                                                                                                          |
|----------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| `text-display` | `clamp(2.125rem, 1.4rem + 3.2vw, 4.25rem)` / 1.05                                                                                                                             |
| `text-heading` | `clamp(1.75rem, 1.35rem + 1.6vw, 2.5rem)` / 1.15                                                                                                                              |
| `text-title`   | `1.25rem` / 1.3                                                                                                                                                               |
| `text-xs`      | `0.8125rem` / 1.125rem: dates, labels and chips. Nothing that is read goes below 13px; only the axis labels inside the journey's SVG charts do, and they scale with the chart |
| Body           | `1rem` / 1.6                                                                                                                                                                  |

Only the Latin subsets are bundled, and the web fonts load with the JavaScript after the first paint
(`src/lib/fonts.ts`). Until they arrive, text uses the faces in `src/styles/fallback-fonts.css`: Arial, Times New
Roman and Courier New (or their metric twins Liberation Sans, Serif and Mono) with `size-adjust` and ascent/descent
overrides measured against each web font, so the swap does not move the layout (CLS 0). The four web fonts are loaded
with the `FontFace` API and added to `document.fonts` together once all of them have loaded, so the page lays out
again only once and no style is recalculated.

Charts that tell categories apart, such as the commit areas in the GitHub metrics, use `chart-1` to `chart-6`: the
cobalt first, then mint, amber, lilac and two neutrals, each with a light and a dark half. They never carry
text; each bar has a labeled legend or row next to it.

## Layout, shape and motion

- `container-page`: `clamp(72rem, 82vw, 96rem)` with a fluid `clamp(1rem, 4vw, 2rem)` gutter. It stays at 72rem up
  to a 1440px viewport and then grows with the screen, so wide monitors get wider grids instead of wider margins.
  Prose keeps a reading measure inside it (`max-w-2xl` to `max-w-4xl`); case study pages, which read like
  articles, stop at 80rem.
- `section`: vertical rhythm of `clamp(3.5rem, 2.5rem + 3.2vw, 6rem)` with `overflow-x: clip` to prevent horizontal
  bleed without disabling `position: sticky`. A home section off screen on phones skips style and layout
  (`content-visibility: auto`) and reserves a safe measured height (`components/layout/Section.tsx`).
- Hero & flow: from 64rem wide and 40rem tall, the hero opens as a centered frame capped at `min(100dvh, 54rem)` with
  `grid-template-columns: minmax(0, 1fr)`. Every section below flows naturally without forced `100dvh` traps per card
  or artificial pagination breaks, preventing oversized cards and empty voids across laptops and tall screens.
- In-page links (`lib/anchors.ts`): a click on a link to a part of the page travels there itself instead of letting the
  browser jump. It lays every section out (`data-traveling`, `data-traveled`), scrolls smoothly so the target aligns
  right beneath the fixed header (`scroll-padding-top: var(--header-height)`), and holds it steady across layout
  frames. Any input from the reader cancels the active trip and hands control back at once.
- Radii: `sm` 0.5rem, `md` 0.75rem (inputs), `lg` 1.25rem (tiles on phones, cards), `xl` 1.75rem (tiles, panels), `2xl`
  2.5rem (the bench, large panels). Buttons and chips are pills.
- Shadows: `shadow-card` for elevation (the tiles' labels, the board's device labels, the bench's labels), `shadow-glow`
  for
  what floats highest (the menu panel). Both are soft and neutral, stronger in the dark theme.
- Motion: `--duration-fast` 120ms, `--duration-base` 200ms, `--duration-slow` 400ms, `ease-standard`,
  `ease-emphasized` and `ease-spring` (a settle with a touch of spring for what lands). Nothing that can be the largest
  paint animates its opacity (on the home that is the hero's
  portrait), so the LCP is never delayed, nothing moves on its own for more than five seconds, and
  `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce` turns every animation and transition off. The new rules below sit inside
  `@media (prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference)`, so they are never declared for that reader at all.
- The hero: as it leaves the screen, its portrait drifts up 2.5rem and dims (`hero-portrait`, the exit range of its
  view timeline).
- Screens: a screen the reader reaches before it has arrived is marked `data-loading` by `CaseImage` and pulses in
  `surface-raised` (four beats at most); on arrival it is marked `data-loaded` and fades in. One that arrives before it
  is reached, or the one a page opens with (`eager`), shows as it is. Around the image, the `picture` carries the
  reveal: a screen on a project or detail page paints in from its top edge (`screen-unmask`, a `clip-path` on the
  picture, never on the
  link, so the link's focus ring stays whole). A frame that clips them uses `overflow: clip`: `overflow: hidden` would
  make it a scroll container, and the view timeline would follow it instead of the page.
- Charts: the journey map rises into place as one piece, like any other block (`section-enter` on its frame); nothing
  inside it is clipped, swept or popped in. The focus
  radar powers on when its tab opens: rings grow from the center (`radar-ring`), then each technology flies out from
  the center (`radar-blip`, `--dx` and `--dy`). The terminal prints its ASCII art one line at a time
  (`ascii-print`, `steps(--ascii-rows)`).
- Sliders on phones: below 48rem the cards at a slider's edges turn away 16° and dim to 0.4 as they enter and leave
  (`carousel-depth`, a `view(inline)` timeline over the track); the card in view is at rest.
- Section entrance: the heading of every home section, the sections of the project and detail pages, the rows of the
  detail indexes and the previous/next cards rise 1.5rem into place as they enter (`section-enter`, a scroll-driven
  animation over the first 40% of their entry). The cards, rows and figures of the home sections do the same: their
  list or grid carries `enter-each`, each part rests after 7rem of scroll, and in a row each one settles 3rem after
  the one before it. One already on screen when the page loads is past that range, so it never starts faded. The bars
  of commits per year grow from the left the same way (`bar-grow`). These rules sit behind
  `@supports ((animation-timeline: view()) and (animation-range: entry))` and take the timeline's own duration
  (`auto`); a slide inside a carousel that scrolls sideways keeps still, since its timeline is the carousel's.
- Figures: the figures under the hero, of the GitHub metrics and of the recommendations (`data-count`) count up from
  zero the first time the reader reaches them (`lib/count-up.ts`). One already on screen when the page settles keeps
  still, and the text ends exactly as it was prerendered.
- Header: a frosted bar at the top of the page that folds once the page scrolls 48px (`data-folded`): the backdrop and
  the sections fade and leave the flow, and two floating frosted pieces stay, the whole name as a pill at the left
  (it never shrinks, so whose page this is never leaves the screen) and a capsule at the right with the theme and the
  round menu button. The header lets the page under its empty part take the pointer. From 80rem the sections sit in
  the unfolded bar; below, and once folded, they live in the menu button's floating panel, which closes with Escape or
  a press outside. A 2px line along the top edge draws the reading progress (`reading-progress`, a scroll timeline, no
  script). The section that crosses the middle of the screen is underlined in the bar and dotted in cobalt in the
  panel, and carries `aria-current`; nothing is marked while the hero is there.
- Between pages: following a link fades from one page to the next where the browser has cross-document view
  transitions, and the header keeps its place (`view-transition-name: site-header`).
- What a control brings in: a tab panel, the list of milestones, an organization's metrics card and the phone menu
  ease in from `@starting-style` (`appear`), and a "Show more" opens to its height where the browser eases to `auto`
  (`.more::details-content`, `interpolate-size`).
- Home layers: the home shows what a recruiter scans in a minute and opens the rest on demand. A job shows two
  achievements that match the role view (up to three) and folds the rest, its stack and its projects behind "Show
  more"; a project is a tile with its illustration, name and a few words, and its page tells the rest; About shows the
  quote and the first paragraph, with "Read the full story". Each of these is a
  native `details` (`components/ui/More.tsx`): find in page opens it, search engines read it, it works before
  hydration. "Expand all" above the experience opens every one at once (`lib/disclosures.ts`). Each service and each
  reason to hire has a page (`/services/{slug}`, `/reasons/{slug}`, a `WebPage` with a `Service` schema for a service)
  under its index (`CollectionPage`); the home names each service by its object, name and few words, and shows the
  reasons as a slide beside their list. Each group of tools has a page too (`/skills/{slug}`, a `WebPage` about a
  `DefinedTerm`): its focus, what it is, what it is good for, all its tools, and the projects, jobs (with the tools of
  the group each one used), programs, certifications and services where it shows (`skillWork` in
  `src/content/shared/skills.ts`). The GitHub metrics have one page (`/metrics`, a `WebPage`), and the home keeps
  the strip of figures. The organizations are named on the home and described on their index.
- Detail pages: a job, a program, an organization, a group of tools, a service and a reason carry their object on its tile beside the
  title (`DetailArticle`'s `art`), square from 48rem and a short band on a phone; their indexes open each row with the
  object. The projects of a job, a program or an organization are tiles (a single project adds its screens), and the
  pages of the services and reasons link jobs, programs, services and reasons as tiles or rows with their objects
  (`views/detail-kit.tsx`).
- Project tiles: a grid, two across on a phone, three from 64rem and four from 96rem; each tile's illustration rises
  onto its layer as the tile comes up (`tile-illustration`, a view timeline). The featured project spans the row.
- Reasons: a sticky slide from 64rem beside the list; the slides share one grid cell and the active one fades in
  (`reason-slide[data-active]`, the others `visibility: hidden`, so assistive technology reads one). One
  `IntersectionObserver` marks the card crossing the middle of the screen, only from 64rem, and that card takes an ink
  border. Each card slides in from the side of the slide as it comes up (a view timeline).
- Pointer: the arrow of a link moves 3px the way it leads, the icon of a link that leaves the site lifts, a download
  drops, and a project tile grows to 1.015, lifts its illustration 8px and leans its arrow wherever the pointer rests
  on it, only under `(hover: hover)`. A "Show more" chevron turns to point where the rows go.
- Experience: an index of rows split by hairlines, the dates and duration in a mono column at the left from 48rem, then
  the title (a link to the job's page), the company, place and mode, the status and one sentence. The achievements,
  the stack and the job's projects (each with its illustration in small) open in place.
- About: from 64rem the story sits beside the terminal and the languages. The terminal holds the ASCII portrait and
  the trajectory as a `cat` of a log, side by side once the terminal itself is 42rem wide (a container query) and
  stacked below that, so the portrait never floats in an empty box. A role view brightens its own steps of the log and
  dims the rest. Education is a timeline on phones and an index two across from 48rem, with the degree on a row of its
  own; each program links to its GitHub organization.
- Skill groups: a gallery of cards standing around a ring that turns one card at a time, every 3.6 s, while it is in
  view (`skill-stage`, `skill-ring`, `skill-card` in `globals.css`; the card is 13.5rem on a phone and up to 17rem,
  the radius follows from the card and the count with `tan()`). Each card is its object on a layer of color, its
  count, its name and its line, and links to the group's page; the cards fade with their distance from the front and
  the ones behind show their hidden back. Previous, pause and next come before the ring; the ring stops under a
  pointer, while a card or an arrow has the focus, off screen and when paused, and a reader who asks for less motion
  gets it paused. Tabbing to a card, clicking one at the side or swiping brings it to the front; a click on the front
  card opens its page. A link under it leads to the index of every group. Certifications
  are index rows two per row from 48rem, so the full list of 29 reads as one index; each
  says what it covered, what it adds today and the journey stop that groups it, with that stop's line keys.
- Figures (the highlights under the hero, the recommendation counts and the GitHub metrics): open strips with no box
  around each number, the number above its label. The strip under the hero shows eight figures chosen per role view,
  four across from 48rem and two on phones. Each column stacks from the top, so the numbers stay on one line
  when a label wraps. On phones the recommendation counts read as lines ("16 Recommendations").
- GitHub metrics: the figure strip, then two panels side by side from 64rem (where the commits are, as one stacked
  bar in `chart-1` to `chart-6` with a legend row per area; and hours versus commits, two thin bars per language),
  then the years as columns from 64rem and as rows with horizontal bars below it, then the weekdays, the editors and
  the notes on repositories and reviews. Every bar has its number in text beside it.
- Resume: the choices and the preview are two columns of fixed measure (34rem and 28rem) centered together. One
  sheet is drawn behind the preview for every extra page (up to four), offset 10px each, with "Page 1 of N" under
  the stack, so the length of each version shows at a glance.
- Services: no card and no list of points on the home; a service's page lists what it covers with checks on its own
  color, then the project tiles that prove it, the jobs it was done in and the reasons that go with it, so every
  promise points to evidence.
- Contact: a `pair` section, the title, the ways to reach me under it, and the form beside them with its top level with
  the title.
- Floating buttons (WhatsApp and the assistant): on phones they step aside while the hero's two buttons sit in the
  bottom 9.5rem of the screen, where they would cover them, and while the contact section is on screen.
- Recommendations: a quote longer than six lines at the card's width shows a "Show more" toggle; the full text
  stays in the page, word for word.
- Sliders (`Carousel`): the recommendations show one card per view on phones, two on tablets and three from 64rem. The
  track scrolls sideways with snap
  points, so a swipe moves one card, and the buttons below it do the same with a counter ("4 / 16"). The track hides
  its scrollbar, takes keyboard focus while it scrolls, and keeps every card in the page, so a screen reader reads a
  plain list. The prerendered HTML carries the first three recommendations and the rest arrive with the JavaScript,
  which keeps the page within the HTML budgets checked in `tests/build/build-output.test.ts`.
- Journey charts: nothing scrolls sideways. From 64rem the map is an SVG with the short lane names on its left edge
  (the chips above carry the full ones). It stays quiet, after the reference of a plain subway diagram: a hairline
  rail per lane, the line's own span at 3px and 60% opacity, a dashed year grid, and no text on the plot but the years
  and "today". A main milestone is a ring, a smaller step a dot, and neighbors on a lane keep 5 units between their
  edges (`layoutStations`), so a step that has happened never lands past today. A stop's lanes are joined and ringed
  only while it is selected (faintly while pointed at), and a single tag names the selected or pointed stop half a
  lane below it (`tagLayout`), so it covers no other stop. Every line that is still active runs on to today; the years
  ahead are a faintly tinted zone. Below 64rem, a strip with one dot per stop and previous and next buttons (or a swipe on the details) move one stop
  at a time, and the line chips use one-word names. Picking a line moves to its latest stop when the selected one is
  not on it. The capability heatmap is a table from 64rem and one year at a time below it. Past spans are solid;
  planned ones are dashed, planned stations have dashed outlines and planned heatmap cells are hatched, so the
  difference between fact and plan does
  not depend on color. Every chart has an accessible alternative: stations are
  focusable buttons with the date and title as their name, the map has a list view, the heatmap is a table, and the
  radar is mirrored by lists of buttons.

- Case study diagrams (`LayeredDiagram`): plain HTML, not SVG. Columns of boxes left to right on wide screens and
  stacked on phones, with decorative arrows between neighbors; the caption states how data flows, so the markup is
  the accessible version. An optional dashed row underneath holds what runs under every column, such as delivery.
- Project pages (case studies and the lighter pages alike): from 80rem (1280px) on, the overview, the figures and an
  "On this page" index sit in a 20rem column beside the text; the index stays in view while reading. Below that the
  overview comes first. Every page ends with the previous and next project, as two cards, and a link to the index.
  The count beside a heading (projects in a category, certifications of an issuer) sits next to it, outside the
  `h2`, so a heading keeps one typeface.
- Detail pages (jobs, programs, certifications, skills, organizations, services and reasons) share that layout
  (`components/page/PageParts.tsx`, `views/detail-kit.tsx`) and add a breadcrumb above the title: the profile section
  they come from, the collection's index and the page. Titles longer than 28 characters beside an illustration (or 40
  without one) take the heading size instead of the display size, and a dash between two names stays with the word
  before it. Timelines are a vertical hairline with a dot per step, oldest first, and steps that have a page of their
  own are links. Running text keeps a 68-character measure. Certifications are grouped by issuer or by year, and open
  their external credentials on Google Drive or the issuer's verification page rather than hosting document scans on
  the site. Commits per year are horizontal bars in `chart-1` on a `surface-raised` track, with the number beside each
  bar, so the figure never depends on the bar. Lists of related pages are index rows or illustrated rows in a bordered
  surface; recommendations reuse the slider.
- Project screens (`CaseImages`): on a project's page, a wide first screenshot spans the page and the rest go two
  across, or full width when only one follows; phone screenshots (taller than wide) go three across at any width,
  centered within 48rem. An image that needs attribution, such as map data, carries a `credit` that renders as a linked
  caption, and a recreated screen of a private project carries `recreation`, captioned as fictional data.
- Open Graph images (`scripts/generate-og.mjs`, `scripts/og/template.html`): every prerendered route has a 1200 × 630
  card in `public/og/` that follows the monochrome Paper/Ink surface and layered tile system: the technical hairline
  grid, an eyebrow in Source Code Pro with a status green or cobalt dot, a two-tone heading in DM Serif Text 400 (`fg`
  and `fg-subtle`), an ink primary pill (`sebastianlopezo.page`) next to a `surface-raised` context pill, and a rounded
  square tile on the right holding the hero board with its socketed portrait on the home cards or the page's own
  hardware illustration on its `tile-*` layer on every inner page.

## Rules

1. Use semantic tokens (`text-fg-muted`, `bg-surface`), never scale steps, in components.
2. Text never sits on `border` or on a chart series that carries a legend instead of an inline label.
3. Every interactive element shows the `ring` focus outline and has a touch target of at least 24px.
4. New colors go through `tokens.css` and `CONTRAST_PAIRS` in the check script.
5. `cn()` (`src/lib/utils.ts`) joins class names and skips the falsy ones a condition leaves; it does not resolve
   conflicts. A component and the `class` its caller passes never set the same property, and each conditional branch
   carries its whole value (`font-normal` on one side, `font-semibold` on the other). Dropping `tailwind-merge` took
   8.6 KB off the startup JavaScript, and the local helper replaces `clsx`.

# Maintenance

The site is only as good as its facts, so it needs a short routine: a checklist before every release and a monthly
pass over the figures, credentials and text.

## Before each release

1. `pnpm lint && pnpm typecheck && pnpm test && pnpm check:contrast && pnpm build && pnpm test:dist && pnpm test:e2e`
2. `pnpm check:links` loads the content modules, adds the repository links the archive builds, and requests every
   external URL, two at a time per site. A 404, a 5xx or a network error fails the run. Sites that block scripts
   (LinkedIn answers 999, Stack Overflow and CodePen answer 403) are listed as unverifiable: open them in a browser.
3. After the deploy, open the home page in both languages, one role view with `?locked=true`, the projects index and
   one case study, and check that the **Production Checks** workflow (Lighthouse) stays in its usual range.

## Every month

1. **Figures.** The GitHub totals and the WakaTime time come from `SebastianLopezO/SebastianLopezO`'s `stats.json`
   and refresh on every CI build; run `pnpm metrics` to commit a newer snapshot. Count the commits by area again
   (`src/content/shared/github.ts`), measure the case study figures the way `docs/content.md` describes (GitHub API,
   `grep` on the tests, the observability config), update `src/content/shared/case-studies.ts` and change the dates
   in `docs/content.md`.
2. **Credentials and recommendations.** Compare a fresh LinkedIn export (`Certifications.csv`,
   `Recommendations_Received.csv`) with `certifications.ts` and `testimonials.ts`. A new certificate needs the page
   that verifies it; a new recommendation is quoted word for word, with its English translation in
   `en/testimonials.ts`.
3. **Profiles.** Check that LinkedIn, HackerRank, freeCodeCamp and Replit show the same headline, current jobs and
   dates as the site, and that the profiles linked from it are public.
4. **Dependencies.** Review Dependabot alerts and pull requests, and `pnpm outdated`.
5. **Review.** Run the recruiter and hiring-manager reviews over the rendered English text. Every sentence that
   changes goes through the humanizer and the Deep fact-check described in `docs/content.md`.

The years of experience need nothing: they are computed from the first job at build time.

## Screenshots

Take product screens only from the local demo stacks with their seed accounts (`docs/content.md` lists how each set
was taken). Put the sources in `assets-src/projects/` and run `pnpm images`. The AVIF encoder is not deterministic, so
the run also rewrites images that did not change; restore them with
`git checkout -- public/cv/previews src/assets/images` before committing.

## Budgets

`pnpm test:dist` enforces them, gzipped: 110 KiB of JavaScript before hydration, 32 KiB per lazy chunk, 12 KiB per
stylesheet, 24 KiB for everything the first paint needs (the head with its inlined styles, the hero and its figures,
which then arrive within two TCP round trips) and 96 KiB per prerendered page (three round trips). Only the hero and the
figures under it, the header and the assistant's launcher hydrate once the page has loaded and painted
(`client:settled` in `src/pages/[...path].astro`): every other home section is an island that loads its code and its
copy in chunks of its own as it then comes within 600 px of the screen (`src/islands/parts.ts`, `content/sections.ts`).
The body of a project or detail page is an island of its own, and the assistant's panel loads when it first opens.
When a chunk crosses its budget, split it the same way.

A section reads its copy synchronously, so its lazy chunk resolves only once that copy has arrived:
`components/sections/section-loaders.ts` lists the copy each section reads, its own and the ones it borrows. A section
that starts reading another section's copy must add it there, or it throws when it hydrates. An island's code and copy
load before Solid hydrates it (`src/islands/client.ts`), which then takes over its prerendered HTML without re-creating
the DOM.

FILE: e2e/anchors.spec.ts

import type {Page} from "@playwright/test";
import {expect, gotoHydrated, test} from "./fixtures";

// How far the section sits from its place right under the header (html's scroll-padding-top).
const distanceFromHeader = (page: Page, id: string) =>
    page.locator(`#${id}`).evaluate((section) =>
        Math.abs(section.getBoundingClientRect().top - parseFloat(getComputedStyle(document.documentElement).scrollPaddingTop)));

test("lands on the section named in the address once the page settles", async ({page}) => {
    await gotoHydrated(page, "/es#metrics");
    await expect.poll(() => distanceFromHeader(page, "metrics")).toBeLessThanOrEqual(1);
});

test("lands on the section of an in-page link across the sections not rendered yet", async ({page}) => {
    await gotoHydrated(page, "/en");
    await page.locator('#home a[href="#contact"]').click();
    await expect(page).toHaveURL(/#contact$/);
    await expect.poll(() => distanceFromHeader(page, "contact")).toBeLessThanOrEqual(1);
});

FILE: e2e/assistant.spec.ts

import type {Page} from "@playwright/test";
import {expect, gotoHydrated, test} from "./fixtures";

// On a phone the floating buttons step aside while the hero's buttons sit under them, so scroll past the hero first,
// to the strip that follows it.
const pastHero = (page: Page) => page.locator("main section").nth(1).scrollIntoViewIfNeeded();

const openAssistant = async (page: Page, lang: "en" | "es") => {
    await page.getByRole("button", {name: lang === "en" ? "Ask about my profile" : "Pregunta sobre mi perfil"}).click();
    const dialog = page.getByRole("dialog", {name: lang === "en" ? "Profile assistant" : "Asistente de perfil"});
    await expect(dialog).toBeVisible();
    return dialog;
};

test("answers questions and returns focus when closed", async ({page, consoleErrors}) => {
    await gotoHydrated(page, "/en");
    await pastHero(page);
    const launcher = page.getByRole("button", {name: "Ask about my profile"});
    const dialog = await openAssistant(page, "en");
    await dialog.getByLabel("Your question").fill("How many years of experience does he have?");
    await dialog.getByRole("button", {name: "Send", exact: true}).click();
    await expect(dialog.getByText(/Sebastián has \d\+ years of experience/)).toBeVisible();
    await page.keyboard.press("Escape");
    await expect(dialog).toBeHidden();
    await expect(launcher).toBeFocused();
    expect(consoleErrors).toEqual([]);
});

test("never offers other role views on locked links", async ({page}) => {
    await gotoHydrated(page, "/es/crm?locked=true");
    await pastHero(page);
    const dialog = await openAssistant(page, "es");
    await dialog.getByLabel("Tu pregunta").fill("¿Encaja en un rol backend?");
    await dialog.getByRole("button", {name: "Enviar", exact: true}).click();
    await expect(dialog.getByText(/Backend es uno de sus perfiles principales/)).toBeVisible();
    // The only internal links allowed are project and detail pages that keep the locked view.
    const routes = await dialog.locator('a[href^="/es/"]').evaluateAll((links) => links.map((link) => link.getAttribute("href")));
    expect(routes.length).toBeGreaterThan(0);
    for (const href of routes) expect(href).toMatch(/^\/es\/(projects|experience|education|certifications|organizations)\/[\w-]+\?locked=true$/);
});

test("follows an answer with questions about the same topic", async ({page, consoleErrors}) => {
    await gotoHydrated(page, "/es");
    await pastHero(page);
    const dialog = await openAssistant(page, "es");
    const suggestions = dialog.getByRole("list", {name: "Preguntas sugeridas"});
    await suggestions.getByRole("button", {name: "¿Quién es Sebastián?"}).click();
    await expect(dialog.getByText(/^Sebastián López Osorno es desarrollador backend y de integraciones/)).toBeVisible();
    // The question just asked leaves the list, and the follow-ups about his story take its place.
    await expect(suggestions.getByRole("button", {name: "¿Quién es Sebastián?"})).toHaveCount(0);
    await suggestions.getByRole("button", {name: "¿Cómo ha sido su trayectoria?"}).click();
    await expect(dialog.getByText(/^En sus palabras: «/)).toBeVisible();
    await expect(dialog.getByRole("link", {name: "Toda la experiencia"})).toHaveAttribute("href", "/es/experience");
    expect(consoleErrors).toEqual([]);
});

test("opens the catalog of questions by topic and answers one about a job", async ({page}) => {
    await gotoHydrated(page, "/es");
    await pastHero(page);
    const dialog = await openAssistant(page, "es");
    const toggle = dialog.getByRole("button", {name: "Más preguntas"});
    await toggle.click();
    await expect(dialog.getByRole("button", {name: "Menos preguntas"})).toHaveAttribute("aria-expanded", "true");
    const catalog = dialog.getByRole("region", {name: "Experiencia"});
    await expect(dialog.getByRole("heading", {level: 3})).toHaveCount(8);
    await catalog.getByRole("button", {name: "¿Qué hizo en Quipux?"}).click();
    await expect(dialog.getByText(/^Analista de Datos \(Práctica\) en Quipux S\.A\.S \(Ago 2022 – May 2023\)\./)).toBeVisible();
    await expect(dialog.getByRole("link", {name: "Quipux S.A.S"})).toHaveAttribute("href", "/es/experience/quipux");
    // Asking closes the catalog again, so the answer has the room.
    await expect(dialog.getByRole("button", {name: "Más preguntas"})).toHaveAttribute("aria-expanded", "false");
});

test("opens the page an answer links to and closes itself", async ({page, consoleErrors}) => {
    await gotoHydrated(page, "/en");
    await pastHero(page);
    const dialog = await openAssistant(page, "en");
    await dialog.getByLabel("Your question").fill("Does he have a Python certification?");
    await dialog.getByRole("button", {name: "Send", exact: true}).click();
    await expect(dialog.getByText(/^Yes\. He holds the IT Specialist – Python/)).toBeVisible();
    await dialog.getByRole("link", {name: "IT Specialist – Python"}).click();
    await expect(page).toHaveURL(/\/en\/certifications\/it-specialist-python$/);
    await expect(dialog).toBeHidden();
    await expect(page.getByRole("heading", {level: 1})).toHaveText("IT Specialist – Python");
    expect(consoleErrors).toEqual([]);
});

test("answers on a detail page and sends section links back to the profile", async ({page, consoleErrors}) => {
    await gotoHydrated(page, "/en/experience/adcom?from=data");
    const dialog = await openAssistant(page, "en");
    await dialog.getByLabel("Your question").fill("Can I download his resume?");
    await dialog.getByRole("button", {name: "Send", exact: true}).click();
    await expect(dialog.getByText(/^You can download his resume/)).toBeVisible();
    const resume = dialog.getByRole("link", {name: "Resume", exact: true});
    await expect(resume).toHaveAttribute("href", "/en/data#resume");
    await resume.click();
    await expect(page).toHaveURL(/\/en\/data#resume$/);
    expect(consoleErrors).toEqual([]);
});

test("keeps the suggested questions within the panel's width", async ({page}) => {
    await gotoHydrated(page, "/en/fullstack");
    await pastHero(page);
    const dialog = await openAssistant(page, "en");
    await dialog.getByRole("button", {name: "More questions"}).click();
    for (const list of await dialog.locator("ul").all()) {
        expect(await list.evaluate((element) => element.scrollWidth - element.clientWidth)).toBeLessThanOrEqual(0);
    }
});

import {expect, gotoHydrated, hydrateSection, test} from "./fixtures";

test("copies the email address and announces it", async ({page, context, consoleErrors}) => {
    await context.grantPermissions(["clipboard-read", "clipboard-write"]);
    await gotoHydrated(page, "/en");
    const contact = await hydrateSection(page, "contact");
    const address = await contact.locator('a[href^="mailto:"]').textContent();
    await contact.getByRole("button", {name: "Copy email address"}).click();
    await expect(contact.getByRole("status")).toHaveText("Email address copied");
    expect(await page.evaluate(() => navigator.clipboard.readText())).toBe(address);
    expect(consoleErrors).toEqual([]);
});

test("moves the floating buttons aside while the contact section is on a phone screen", async ({page, isMobile}) => {
    test.skip(!isMobile, "Wide screens leave a margin beside the content");
    await gotoHydrated(page, "/en");
    const whatsapp = page.locator('a[aria-label="Chat on WhatsApp"]');
    const assistant = page.locator('button[aria-label="Ask about my profile"]');
    // The buttons also step aside while the hero's buttons sit under them, so start past the hero.
    const pastHero = page.locator("main section").nth(1);
    await pastHero.scrollIntoViewIfNeeded();
    await expect(whatsapp).toBeVisible();
    await page.locator("#contact form").scrollIntoViewIfNeeded();
    await expect(whatsapp).toBeHidden();
    await expect(assistant).toBeHidden();
    await pastHero.scrollIntoViewIfNeeded();
    await expect(whatsapp).toBeVisible();
    await expect(assistant).toBeVisible();
});

test("keeps the floating buttons off the hero's buttons on a phone", async ({page, isMobile}) => {
    test.skip(!isMobile, "Wide screens keep the hero's buttons on the left");
    const actions = page.getByRole("link", {name: "Contact me"});
    const whatsapp = page.locator('a[aria-label="Chat on WhatsApp"]');
    for (const height of [640, 740, 915]) {
        await page.setViewportSize({width: 393, height});
        await gotoHydrated(page, "/en");
        const fab = await whatsapp.elementHandle();
        // The button fades out over 200ms and only turns hidden at the end, so wait for it to settle.
        await expect.poll(() => actions.evaluate((link, button) => {
            const a = link.getBoundingClientRect();
            const b = button!.getBoundingClientRect();
            return getComputedStyle(button!).visibility !== "hidden" && a.top < b.bottom && a.bottom > b.top && a.left < b.right && a.right > b.left;
        }, fab), {message: `393x${height}`}).toBe(false);
    }
});

test("checks the required fields before opening WhatsApp or the mail app", async ({page}) => {
    await gotoHydrated(page, "/es");
    const contact = page.locator("#contact");
    await expect(contact.getByRole("button", {name: "Enviar por WhatsApp"})).toBeVisible();
    await contact.getByRole("button", {name: "Enviar por correo"}).click();
    expect(await page.locator("#contact-name").evaluate((input: HTMLInputElement) => input.validity.valueMissing)).toBe(true);
    await expect(page).toHaveURL(/\/es$/);
});

import {expect, gotoHydrated, hydrateSection, test} from "./fixtures";

test("lays the profile out across a wide screen", async ({page, isMobile}) => {
    test.skip(isMobile, "Wide screens only");
    await page.setViewportSize({width: 1920, height: 1080});
    await gotoHydrated(page, "/en");
    const container = await page.locator("#experience .container-page").boundingBox();
    expect(container!.width).toBeGreaterThanOrEqual(1920 * 0.75);
    // Each job spans the container instead of half of it.
    const job = await page.locator("#experience-jobs > li").first().boundingBox();
    expect(job!.width).toBeGreaterThan(container!.width * 0.8);
});

test("shortens long recommendations and opens them on request", async ({page}) => {
    await gotoHydrated(page, "/en");
    await hydrateSection(page, "testimonials");
    const toggle = page.locator("#testimonials").getByRole("button", {name: "Show more"}).first();
    await expect(toggle).toHaveAttribute("aria-expanded", "false");
    const quote = page.locator(`#${await toggle.getAttribute("aria-controls")}`);
    const clamped = await quote.evaluate((element) => element.clientHeight);
    await toggle.click();
    await expect(page.locator("#testimonials").getByRole("button", {name: "Show less"}).first()).toHaveAttribute("aria-expanded", "true");
    expect(await quote.evaluate((element) => element.clientHeight)).toBeGreaterThan(clamped);
});

test("keeps the case study overview and index beside the text on wide screens", async ({page, isMobile}) => {
    test.skip(isMobile, "Wide screens only");
    await page.setViewportSize({width: 1440, height: 900});
    await gotoHydrated(page, "/en/projects/smartpot");
    const overview = await page.getByRole("complementary", {name: "At a glance"}).boundingBox();
    const problem = await page.locator("#case-problem").boundingBox();
    expect(overview!.x).toBeGreaterThan(problem!.x + problem!.width);
    const index = page.getByRole("navigation", {name: "On this page"});
    await expect(index).toBeVisible();
    await expect(index.getByRole("link", {name: "Results"})).toHaveAttribute("href", "#case-results");
});

test("shows one recommendation at a time on phones and moves with the buttons", async ({page, isMobile}) => {
    test.skip(!isMobile, "Phones only");
    await gotoHydrated(page, "/en");
    const section = await hydrateSection(page, "testimonials");
    const track = section.locator("ul").first();
    await expect(track.locator(":scope > li")).toHaveCount(16);
    const card = await track.locator(":scope > li").first().boundingBox();
    const box = await track.boundingBox();
    expect(card!.width).toBeGreaterThan(box!.width * 0.75);
    expect(card!.width).toBeLessThan(box!.width);

    await section.getByRole("button", {name: "Next recommendations"}).click();
    await expect.poll(() => track.evaluate((element) => element.scrollLeft)).toBeGreaterThan(card!.width * 0.5);
    await expect(section.getByRole("button", {name: "Previous recommendations"})).toBeEnabled();
});

import {expect, gotoHydrated, test} from "./fixtures";

const DETAILS: Record<string, string[]> = {
    experience: ["tivenos", "adcom", "muv-u", "quipux"],
    education: ["computer-engineering", "cybersecurity-diploma", "programming-technician", "pascual-bravo", "inem"],
    certifications: [
        "it-specialist-python", "dax-power-bi", "power-bi-analysis", "data-science-ai", "cybersecurity", "problem-solving", "excel-mastery",
        "excel-data-analysis", "search-console-seo", "green-digital-skills", "data-visualization", "web-programming", "iot-protocols", "git-github",
        "software-engineering", "django-two", "practical-javascript", "basic-programming", "python-fundamentals", "hacklab", "java-basic", "css",
        "python-django", "python-basic", "excel-professional", "sql-basic", "programming-fundamentals", "python-eia", "html",
    ],
    organizations: [
        "tivenoseducation", "adcom-group", "smartpottech", "gopoli", "peppertechdev", "engineeringsebastian-s", "taurussebastian-s", "testlabdata",
        "technicalsebastians", "vocationalsebastian-s",
    ],
    skills: [
        "backend-and-apis", "crm-and-automation", "data-and-business-intelligence", "devops-and-observability", "databases",
        "frontend", "cloud-and-hosting", "testing-and-quality", "programming-languages", "security", "machine-learning-and-ai",
        "iot-and-embedded", "networking", "developer-tools", "computer-science-foundations",
    ],
};

// Every English page and both languages' indexes; the Spanish pages share the components and are checked below.
const PATHS = [
    ...Object.entries(DETAILS).flatMap(([collection, slugs]) => [`/en/${collection}`, ...slugs.map((slug) => `/en/${collection}/${slug}`)]),
    ...Object.keys(DETAILS).map((collection) => `/es/${collection}`),
];

for (const path of PATHS) {
    test(`renders and hydrates ${path}`, async ({page, consoleErrors}) => {
        await gotoHydrated(page, path);
        await expect(page.getByRole("heading", {level: 1})).toBeVisible();
        await expect(page.getByRole("navigation", {name: "Breadcrumb"}).or(page.getByRole("navigation", {name: "Ruta de navegación"}))).toBeVisible();
        expect(consoleErrors).toEqual([]);
    });
}

test("opens a job page from the home page and keeps the locked role view", async ({page, consoleErrors}) => {
    await gotoHydrated(page, "/en/backend?locked=true");
    await page.locator("#experience").getByRole("link", {name: "Read the full experience"}).first().click();
    await expect(page).toHaveURL(/\/en\/experience\/[a-z-]+\?from=backend&locked=true$/);
    await expect(page.getByRole("heading", {level: 2, name: "What I did"})).toBeVisible();
    const breadcrumb = page.getByRole("navigation", {name: "Breadcrumb"});
    await expect(breadcrumb.getByRole("link", {name: "Home"})).toHaveAttribute("href", "/en/backend?locked=true#experience");
    await expect(breadcrumb.getByRole("link", {name: "Professional experience"})).toHaveAttribute("href", "/en/experience?locked=true");
    await breadcrumb.getByRole("link", {name: "Professional experience"}).click();
    await expect(page).toHaveURL(/\/en\/experience\?from=backend&locked=true$/);
    await expect(page.getByRole("heading", {level: 1})).toHaveText("Professional experience");
    expect(consoleErrors).toEqual([]);
});

test("tells a job with its titles, timeline, projects and recommendations", async ({page}) => {
    await gotoHydrated(page, "/en/experience/adcom");
    await expect(page.getByRole("heading", {level: 1})).toHaveText("ADCOM GROUP");
    const titles = page.locator('section[aria-labelledby="detail-positions"] li');
    await expect(titles).toHaveCount(2);
    await expect(titles.first()).toContainText("Feb 2025 – Jun 2025");
    const timeline = page.locator('section[aria-labelledby="detail-timeline"]');
    await expect(timeline).toContainText("Became CRM Developer · MarTech Developer · CRM & Cloud Solutions Engineer");
    await expect(timeline.getByRole("link", {name: "Hyper-Personalized Email at Scale begins"})).toHaveAttribute("href", "/en/projects/email-automations");
    // Each project appears as its illustrated tile, linking to its project page.
    const projects = page.locator('section[aria-labelledby="detail-projects"]');
    await expect(projects.locator("a:has(img)")).toHaveCount(5);
    await expect(page.locator('section[aria-labelledby="detail-recommendations"] figure')).toHaveCount(2);
    await expect(page.getByRole("link", {name: "ADCOM-Group"}).first()).toHaveAttribute("href", "/en/organizations/adcom-group");
});

test("lists what was studied during a job", async ({page}) => {
    await gotoHydrated(page, "/es/experience/muv-u");
    const studied = page.locator('section[aria-labelledby="detail-meanwhile"]');
    await expect(studied.getByRole("heading", {name: "Lo que estudiaba mientras tanto"})).toBeVisible();
    await expect(studied.getByRole("link", {name: /IT Specialist – Python/})).toHaveAttribute("href", "/es/certifications/it-specialist-python");
    expect(await studied.getByRole("link").count()).toBeGreaterThan(10);
});

test("copies a page's link with its role view", async ({page, context, consoleErrors}) => {
    await context.grantPermissions(["clipboard-read", "clipboard-write"]);
    await gotoHydrated(page, "/en/experience/adcom?from=crm");
    await page.getByRole("button", {name: "Copy link"}).click();
    await expect(page.getByRole("button", {name: "Link copied"})).toBeVisible();
    expect(await page.evaluate(() => navigator.clipboard.readText())).toBe(new URL("/en/experience/adcom?from=crm", page.url()).href);
    expect(consoleErrors).toEqual([]);
});

test("groups the certifications by issuer or by year", async ({page, consoleErrors}) => {
    await gotoHydrated(page, "/en/certifications");
    const grouping = page.getByRole("group", {name: "Group the certifications"});
    await grouping.and(page.locator("[data-interactive]")).waitFor({state: "attached"});
    await expect(page.getByRole("heading", {level: 2, name: "Platzi"})).toBeVisible();
    await grouping.getByRole("button", {name: "By year"}).click();
    await expect(grouping.getByRole("button", {name: "By year"})).toHaveAttribute("aria-pressed", "true");
    await expect(page.getByRole("heading", {level: 2, name: "2024"})).toBeVisible();
    await expect(page.getByRole("heading", {level: 2, name: "Platzi"})).toHaveCount(0);
    await expect(page.locator('section[aria-labelledby^="year-"] li h3')).toHaveCount(29);
    await grouping.getByRole("button", {name: "By issuer"}).click();
    await expect(page.getByRole("heading", {level: 2, name: "Platzi"})).toBeVisible();
    expect(consoleErrors).toEqual([]);
});

test("filters a job's timeline by kind and groups it by year", async ({page, consoleErrors}) => {
    await gotoHydrated(page, "/es/experience/muv-u");
    const timeline = page.locator('section[aria-labelledby="detail-timeline"]');
    const filter = timeline.getByRole("group", {name: "Filtrar la cronología"});
    await filter.and(page.locator("[data-interactive]")).waitFor({state: "attached"});
    const entries = timeline.locator("ol ol > li");
    const total = await entries.count();
    await expect(timeline.getByRole("heading", {level: 3, name: "2023"})).toBeVisible();
    await filter.getByRole("button", {name: /^Certificaciones/}).click();
    await expect(filter.getByRole("button", {name: /^Certificaciones/})).toHaveAttribute("aria-pressed", "true");
    const certificates = await entries.count();
    expect(certificates).toBeGreaterThan(10);
    expect(certificates).toBeLessThan(total);
    await expect(timeline.getByRole("link", {name: "Obtuve la certificación IT Specialist – Python"})).toHaveAttribute("href", "/es/certifications/it-specialist-python");
    await filter.getByRole("button", {name: /^Todo/}).click();
    await expect(entries).toHaveCount(total);
    expect(consoleErrors).toEqual([]);
});

test("shows an organization's activity, projects and public repositories", async ({page}) => {
    await gotoHydrated(page, "/en/organizations/smartpottech");
    const activity = page.locator('section[aria-labelledby="detail-activity"]');
    await expect(activity).toContainText("2,629 of 2,836 commits");
    await expect(activity).toContainText("93% of the commits made by people");

FILE: e2e/fixtures.ts

import {expect, type Page, test as base} from "@playwright/test";

const THIRD_PARTY = /googletagmanager\.com|google-analytics\.com|raw\.githubusercontent\.com/;

export const test = base.extend<{ consoleErrors: string[] }>({
    consoleErrors: async ({page}, use) => {
        const errors: string[] = [];
        await page.route(THIRD_PARTY, (route) => route.abort());
        page.on("console", (message) => {
            if (message.type() === "error" && !message.text().includes("net::ERR_FAILED")) errors.push(message.text());
        });
        page.on("pageerror", (error) => errors.push(error.message));
        await use(errors);
    },
});

export {expect};

export const ROLES = ["backend", "crm", "data", "devops", "fullstack"] as const;

export const PAGES = ["en", "es"].flatMap((lang) => [`/${lang}`, ...ROLES.map((role) => `/${lang}/${role}`)]);

export const gotoHydrated = async (page: Page, path: string) => {
    await page.goto(path);
    await page.locator('html[data-hydrated="true"]').waitFor({state: "attached"});
};

/**
 * A home section is an island that hydrates as it comes near the screen: this brings it there and waits until it
 * responds, as a reader scrolling to it would find it.
 */
export const hydrateSection = async (page: Page, id: string) => {
    const section = page.locator(`section#${id}`);
    await section.scrollIntoViewIfNeeded();
    await page.locator(`section#${id}[data-hydrated="true"]`).waitFor({state: "attached"});
    return section;
};

import type {Page} from "@playwright/test";

const openJourney = async (page: Page, path: string) => {
    await gotoHydrated(page, path);
    await hydrateSection(page, "journey");
    const tabs = page.locator('#journey [role="tablist"]');
    await tabs.and(page.locator("[data-interactive]")).waitFor({state: "attached"});
    return tabs;
};

    test.skip(!isMobile, "Phones only");
    await openJourney(page, "/en");
    const heading = page.locator("#journey-panel-map").getByRole("heading", {level: 3});

    await expect(heading).not.toHaveText(first!);
    await page.getByRole("button", {name: "Next stop"}).click();

        [...section.querySelectorAll<HTMLElement>("*")].filter((element) =>
            /(auto|scroll)/.test(getComputedStyle(element).overflowX) && element.scrollWidth > element.clientWidth + 1 && element.offsetParent !== null).length);
    expect(sideways).toBe(0);
});

FILE: e2e/layout.spec.ts

import {expect, test} from "./fixtures";

const VIEWPORTS = [
    {width: 360, height: 780},
    {width: 768, height: 1024},
    {width: 1440, height: 900},
];

for (const viewport of VIEWPORTS) {
    for (const path of ["/en", "/es/data"]) {
        test(`fits ${path} in a ${viewport.width}px viewport without clipped content`, async ({page}) => {
            await page.setViewportSize(viewport);
            await page.goto(path);

            const overflow = await page.evaluate(() => document.documentElement.scrollWidth - window.innerWidth);
            expect(overflow).toBeLessThanOrEqual(0);

            const ascii = page.locator("#about pre");
            await expect(ascii).toBeVisible();
            const asciiFits = await ascii.evaluate((element) => {
                const box = element.getBoundingClientRect();
                const frame = element.parentElement!.getBoundingClientRect();
                return element.scrollWidth <= element.clientWidth + 1 && box.left >= frame.left - 1 && box.right <= frame.right + 1;
            });
            expect(asciiFits).toBe(true);

            const photo = page.locator("#home picture img");
            await photo.scrollIntoViewIfNeeded();
            await expect.poll(() => photo.evaluate((image: HTMLImageElement) => image.complete && image.naturalWidth > 0)).toBe(true);
        });
    }
}

for (const viewport of VIEWPORTS) {
    for (const path of [
        "/en/projects", "/es/projects/integration-platform", "/en/projects/smartpot", "/es/projects/computer-engineering",
        "/es/experience/tivenos", "/en/education/computer-engineering", "/en/certifications/search-console-seo", "/es/organizations/engineeringsebastian-s",
        "/en/certifications",
    ]) {
        test(`fits ${path} in a ${viewport.width}px viewport`, async ({page}) => {
            await page.setViewportSize(viewport);
            await page.goto(path);
            const overflow = await page.evaluate(() => document.documentElement.scrollWidth - window.innerWidth);
            expect(overflow).toBeLessThanOrEqual(0);
        });
    }
}

import {expect, gotoHydrated, hydrateSection, test} from "./fixtures";

const opacityOf = (element: Element) => Number(getComputedStyle(element).opacity);

test("folds the header as the page scrolls and marks the section being read in its menu", async ({
                                                                                                     page,
                                                                                                     consoleErrors
                                                                                                 }) => {
    await gotoHydrated(page, "/en");
    const header = page.locator(".site-header");
    await expect(header).not.toHaveAttribute("data-folded");
    await expect(page.locator('.site-header a[aria-current="true"]')).toHaveCount(0);
    await hydrateSection(page, "experience");
    await page.locator("#experience h2").scrollIntoViewIfNeeded();
    // Once the reader scrolls, the bar folds into the floating name and controls capsule, and the menu lists the sections.
    await expect(header).toHaveAttribute("data-folded", "true");
    await expect(header.getByRole("link", {name: /Sebastián/})).toBeVisible();
    await header.getByRole("button", {name: "Open menu"}).click();
    const menu = page.locator("#site-menu").getByRole("navigation", {name: "Main navigation"});
    await expect(menu.getByRole("link", {name: "Experience"})).toHaveAttribute("aria-current", "true");
    await expect(menu.locator('a[aria-current="true"]')).toHaveCount(1);
    // The mark is not color alone: the current entry carries a dot.
    const dot = menu.getByRole("link", {name: "Experience"}).locator("span[aria-hidden]");
    expect(await dot.evaluate((element) => getComputedStyle(element).backgroundColor)).not.toBe("rgba(0, 0, 0, 0)");
    // Escape closes it and gives the focus back to its button.
    await page.keyboard.press("Escape");
    await expect(page.locator("#site-menu")).toHaveCount(0);
    await expect(header.getByRole("button", {name: "Open menu"})).toBeFocused();
    expect(consoleErrors).toEqual([]);
});

test("switches the theme and remembers it", async ({page}) => {
    await gotoHydrated(page, "/en");
    const html = page.locator("html");
    const toggle = page.locator(".header-controls").getByRole("button", {name: /Switch to the (light|dark) theme/});
    const before = await page.evaluate(() => getComputedStyle(document.body).backgroundColor);
    const next = (await toggle.getAttribute("aria-label"))!.includes("dark") ? "dark" : "light";
    await toggle.click();
    await expect(html).toHaveAttribute("data-theme", next);
    expect(await page.evaluate(() => getComputedStyle(document.body).backgroundColor)).not.toBe(before);
    // The choice holds on the next page, applied before its first paint.
    await page.goto("/en/projects");
    await expect(html).toHaveAttribute("data-theme", next);
});

test("raises the parts of a section as they enter the screen", async ({page}) => {
    await gotoHydrated(page, "/en");
    const figure = page.locator("dl.enter-each").first().locator("> div").first();
    // Below the first screen a part waits faded, and at rest once it is well inside.
    expect(await figure.evaluate(opacityOf)).toBe(0);
    await figure.evaluate((element) => element.scrollIntoView({block: "center"}));
    await expect.poll(() => figure.evaluate(opacityOf)).toBe(1);
});

    await expect.poll(() => figure.textContent(), {intervals: [40]}).not.toBe(written);
    await expect(figure).toHaveText(written!);
});

test("holds the place of a screen that has not arrived and fades it in once it has", async ({page}) => {
    // The project screens are held back until the reader has seen the empty frame, as on a slow connection.
    let arrive!: () => void;
    const arrived = new Promise<void>((resolve) => (arrive = resolve));
    await page.route(/\/projects\/.+\.(avif|webp)$/, async (route) => {
        await arrived;
        await route.continue();
    });
    await gotoHydrated(page, "/en/projects/integration-platform");
    const screen = page.locator("main .screen-unmask img").last();
    await screen.evaluate((element) => element.scrollIntoView({block: "center"}));
    await expect(screen).toHaveAttribute("data-loading", "");
    arrive();
    await expect(screen).toHaveAttribute("data-loaded", "");
    await expect(screen).not.toHaveAttribute("data-loading");
    await expect.poll(() => screen.evaluate(opacityOf)).toBe(1);
});

test("turns the skills gallery one card at a time, and stops when asked", async ({page, consoleErrors}) => {
    await gotoHydrated(page, "/en");
    const section = await hydrateSection(page, "skills");
    const gallery = section.getByRole("region", {name: "Technical skills gallery"});
    const cards = gallery.locator(".skill-card");
    await expect(cards).toHaveCount(15);
    await expect(cards.first()).toHaveAttribute("aria-label", "1 of 15");
    await gallery.locator(".skill-stage").scrollIntoViewIfNeeded();
    // In view it turns by itself, one card per step.
    await expect(cards.nth(1)).toHaveAttribute("data-active", "true", {timeout: 8000});
    await expect(gallery.locator(".skill-card[data-active]")).toHaveCount(1);
    // Paused, it stays; the button then offers to resume.
    await gallery.getByRole("button", {name: "Pause the gallery"}).click();
    const resume = gallery.getByRole("button", {name: "Resume the gallery"});
    await expect(resume).toBeVisible();
    const held = await gallery.locator(".skill-ring").evaluate((ring) => (ring as HTMLElement).style.getPropertyValue("--turn"));
    await page.mouse.move(0, 0);
    await page.waitForTimeout(4500);
    expect(await gallery.locator(".skill-ring").evaluate((ring) => (ring as HTMLElement).style.getPropertyValue("--turn"))).toBe(held);
    // The buttons turn it either way, wrapping around the ring, and tell a screen reader where it stands.
    const active = () => gallery.locator(".skill-card[data-active]").getAttribute("aria-label");
    const before = Number((await active())!.split(" ")[0]);
    await gallery.getByRole("button", {name: "Next skill"}).click();
    await expect.poll(active).toBe(`${(before % 15) + 1} of 15`);
    await gallery.getByRole("button", {name: "Previous skill"}).click();
    await gallery.getByRole("button", {name: "Previous skill"}).click();
    await expect.poll(active).toBe(`${((before - 2 + 15) % 15) + 1} of 15`);
    await expect(gallery.getByRole("status")).toContainText("of 15");
    expect(consoleErrors).toEqual([]);
});

test("brings a side card of the skills gallery to the front before opening it", async ({page, isMobile}) => {
    await gotoHydrated(page, "/en");
    const section = await hydrateSection(page, "skills");
    const gallery = section.getByRole("region", {name: "Technical skills gallery"});
    await gallery.getByRole("button", {name: "Pause the gallery"}).click();
    const stage = gallery.locator(".skill-stage");
    await stage.scrollIntoViewIfNeeded();
    const front = gallery.locator(".skill-card[data-active]");
    const first = await front.getAttribute("aria-label");
    if (isMobile) {
        // A swipe to the left turns the next card to the front.
        const box = (await stage.boundingBox())!;
        await page.mouse.move(box.x + box.width * 0.7, box.y + box.height / 2);
        await page.mouse.down();
        await page.mouse.move(box.x + box.width * 0.2, box.y + box.height / 2, {steps: 6});
        await page.mouse.up();
        await expect(front).not.toHaveAttribute("aria-label", first!);
        return;
    }
    // A click on the card to the right of the front turns it to the front instead of leaving the page.
    const neighbors = await gallery.locator(".skill-card").evaluateAll((cards) => cards
        .filter((card) => (card as HTMLElement).style.getPropertyValue("--d").trim() === "1")
        .map((card) => ({label: card.getAttribute("aria-label"), x: card.getBoundingClientRect().x})));
    expect(neighbors).toHaveLength(2);
    const side = neighbors.sort((a, b) => b.x - a.x)[0];
    const card = gallery.locator(`.skill-card[aria-label="${side.label}"] a`);
    await card.click();
    await expect(page).toHaveURL(/\/en$/);
    await expect(front).toHaveAttribute("aria-label", side.label!);
    // At the front, the same click opens its page.
    await card.click();
    await expect(page).toHaveURL(/\/en\/skills\/[a-z-]+$/);
    await expect(page.getByRole("heading", {level: 2, name: "Focus"})).toBeVisible();
});

// Lighthouse runs on a slow CPU and network, where a body that suspends during hydration swapped the prerendered text
// for an empty fallback until its chunk arrived (CLS above 1).
test("keeps the prerendered case study on screen while it hydrates on a slow device", async ({page}) => {
    const cdp = await page.context().newCDPSession(page);
    await cdp.send("Emulation.setCPUThrottlingRate", {rate: 4});
    await cdp.send("Network.emulateNetworkConditions", {
        offline: false,
        latency: 150,
        downloadThroughput: 200_000,
        uploadThroughput: 90_000
    });
    await page.addInitScript(() => {
        (window as unknown as { shifts: number }).shifts = 0;
        new PerformanceObserver((list) => {
            for (const entry of list.getEntries() as unknown as { value: number; hadRecentInput: boolean }[]) {
                if (!entry.hadRecentInput) (window as unknown as { shifts: number }).shifts += entry.value;
            }
        }).observe({type: "layout-shift", buffered: true});
    });
    await gotoHydrated(page, "/es/projects/smartpot?from=backend&locked=true");
    await page.waitForTimeout(3000);
    expect(await page.evaluate(() => (window as unknown as { shifts: number }).shifts)).toBeLessThan(0.1);
});

test("redirects the root by browser language and keeps the query", async ({request}) => {
    const spanish = await request.get("/?locked=true", {
        headers: {"Accept-Language": "es-CO,es;q=0.9"},
        maxRedirects: 0
    });
    expect(spanish.status()).toBe(302);
    expect(spanish.headers().location).toMatch(/\/es\?locked=true$/);
    const english = await request.get("/", {headers: {"Accept-Language": "en-US"}, maxRedirects: 0});
    expect(english.headers().location).toMatch(/\/en$/);
});

});

================================================
FILE: nginx/default.conf
================================================
map $http_accept_language $preferred_lang {
    default en;
    ~*^es   es;
}

server {
    listen 8080;
    server_name _;
    root /usr/share/nginx/html;
    index index.html;
    charset utf-8;
    server_tokens off;
    absolute_redirect off;

    # The build writes a .br and a .gz next to every text file: Brotli for the browsers that ask for it (about a quarter
    # smaller on the pages), gzip for the rest.
    brotli_static on;
    gzip_static on;
    gzip on;
    gzip_vary on;
    # The host's reverse proxy talks HTTP/1.0 to this container unless it sets proxy_http_version, and nginx only
    # compresses for HTTP/1.1 by default: without these two lines the scripts reach visitors uncompressed.
    gzip_http_version 1.0;
    gzip_proxied any;
    gzip_comp_level 6;
    gzip_min_length 1024;
    gzip_types text/plain text/css text/xml application/javascript application/json application/xml image/svg+xml;

    error_page 404 /404.html;

    # Responses that leave from this level or from a location without add_header of its own (the 405, /health, the
    # trailing-slash 301) take the security headers from here. The locations that set Cache-Control include them again,
    # because a level that adds a header does not inherit the ones above it.
    include /etc/nginx/snippets/security-headers.conf;

    # A static site takes no request bodies and answers only GET and HEAD; short timeouts free slow connections.
    if ($request_method !~ ^(GET|HEAD)$) {
        return 405;
    }
    client_max_body_size 1k;
    client_body_timeout 10s;
    client_header_timeout 10s;
    keepalive_timeout 15s;
    send_timeout 10s;

    location = /health {
        access_log off;
        default_type application/json;
        return 200 '{"status":"UP"}';
    }

    location = / {
        include /etc/nginx/snippets/security-headers.conf;
        add_header Cache-Control "no-cache" always;
        add_header Vary "Accept-Language" always;
        return 302 /$preferred_lang$is_args$args;
    }

    location ~ ^(?<trimmed>/.+?)/+$ {
        return 301 $trimmed$is_args$args;
    }

    # Every page has one address: the file behind it (/en/index.html) moves to the page (/en), and /index.html to /.
    location ~ ^(?<page>/.*?)/?index\.html$ {
        include /etc/nginx/snippets/security-headers.conf;
        return 301 $page$is_args$args;
    }

    # The not-found page answers only as the error of another address; asked for by its name it is not found either.
    location = /404.html {
        internal;
        include /etc/nginx/snippets/security-headers.conf;
        add_header Cache-Control "no-cache" always;
    }

    # Renamed project pages keep answering at their old address.
    location ~ ^/(?<page_lang>en|es)/projects/results-email$ {
        include /etc/nginx/snippets/security-headers.conf;
        return 301 /$page_lang/projects/email-automations$is_args$args;
    }

    location ^~ /assets/ {
        include /etc/nginx/snippets/security-headers.conf;
        add_header Cache-Control "public, max-age=31536000, immutable" always;
        try_files $uri =404;
    }

    location ~* \.(?:pdf|jpe?g|png|webp|avif|svg|ico)$ {
        include /etc/nginx/snippets/security-headers.conf;
        add_header Cache-Control "public, max-age=604800" always;
        try_files $uri =404;
    }

    location ~ ^/(?:robots\.txt|sitemap\.xml)$ {
        include /etc/nginx/snippets/security-headers.conf;
        add_header Cache-Control "public, max-age=3600" always;
        try_files $uri =404;
    }

    location / {
        include /etc/nginx/snippets/security-headers.conf;
        add_header Cache-Control "no-cache" always;
        # The pages are files: the role view (?from=) and the lock (?locked=) change nothing in them, so a page
        # prefetched without them serves the visit that carries them (lib/role-links.ts adds ?from= on the click).
        add_header No-Vary-Search 'params=("from" "locked")' always;
        try_files $uri $uri/index.html =404;
    }
}

FILE: scripts/build.ts

import {build as buildPages} from "astro";
import {build} from "vite";
import {dirname, join} from "node:path";
import {fileURLToPath} from "node:url";
import {refreshGithubStats} from "./github-stats.ts";

process.env.BUILD_DATE ??= new Date().toISOString().slice(0, 10);
const root = join(dirname(fileURLToPath(import.meta.url)), "..");

// CI and the Docker image build with the latest GitHub figures; a local build keeps the committed snapshot.
if (process.env.CI) await refreshGithubStats();

// Astro generates every page; scripts/postbuild.ts then writes what is built from all of them together.
await buildPages({root, logLevel: "warn"});
// The routes, the sitemap and robots builders and the profile come from the same modules as the pages.
await build({
    root,
    configFile: false,
    logLevel: "warn",
    define: {
        __BUILD_DATE__: JSON.stringify(process.env.BUILD_DATE),
        __SITE_URL__: JSON.stringify(process.env.SITE_URL ?? "https://sebastianlopezo.page"),
    },
    resolve: {alias: {"@": join(root, "src")}},
    build: {ssr: "src/build-data.ts", outDir: "dist-ssr", copyPublicDir: false, emptyOutDir: true},
});
await import("./postbuild.ts");
