# Build a popup menu

This guide covers one popup menu: a list of commands or links that users move through with arrow keys. What opens it
does not matter: a button (an "Actions" or overflow button), an item in another menu (a submenu), or no visible trigger
at all (a context menu).

Several triggers on one page are independent menus unless you build a bar: each is its own `Tab` stop, and nothing links
them. A row of menus that act as one widget (File, Edit, View: one `Tab` stop, `ArrowLeft`/`ArrowRight` between them,
hover switching) is an application menu bar. Build each menu as described here, then see `app-menus` (via
`npx -y modern-web-guidance@latest retrieve "app-menus"`) for what links them.

## Commands, links, and what makes a menu

Two independent choices. Everything else here applies to both.

* **Element, per item.** A command is a `<button type="button">`; a destination is an `<a href>` that still opens in a
  new tab, copies as a URL, and works without script. A menu may mix them freely: two links and six commands, or one
  command and six links, changes nothing below.
* **Interaction model, per menu.** Arrow keys, `Home`/`End`, and `Esc` make it a menu: add the focusgroup, let it infer
  `menuitem` on every item whether button or link, and make it look like one (a trigger with a dropdown indicator, or a
  continuous bar for an application menu bar). A short list of links users `Tab` through is navigation: no focusgroup,
  no `role="menu"`, `role="menuitem"`, or `aria-haspopup="menu"`; keep the popover, `Esc`, and focus restoration. For
  navigation, see `navbar` (via `npx -y modern-web-guidance@latest retrieve "navbar"`).

Content never decides the roles. A "Products" dropdown of links can be a menu; an "Account" dropdown of commands cannot
be navigation.

Use the menu pattern only for a composite widget with one tab stop and arrow-key navigation. Use a
`<div focusgroup="menu nomemory">`, not the HTML `<menu>` element. Do not add `role="menu"` or `role="menuitem"` in the
shared markup: native focusgroup infers those roles, and explicit roles block that inference. Add them only in the
unsupported-browser fallback below. `nomemory` makes reopening start at the first item. Focusgroup moves focus; script
handles activation, submenu preview, and focus restoration.

## Open and position the menu

Make each trigger a command invoker with `commandfor` and `command="toggle-popover"`. The browser opens and closes the
popover on click, Enter, and Space, and keeps the trigger inside its popover's light-dismiss group, so clicking an open
trigger closes it. Do not use `popovertarget` or `popovertargetaction`; this pattern uses `commandfor` instead.

Place each popover immediately after its trigger. Browsers add an implicit `aria-details` relationship only when the
popover is not the next sibling, so this placement avoids it without extra attributes.

A menu with no trigger button opens from script with `showPopover({ source })`. `source` sets the implicit anchor, so
pass the element the menu belongs to: the right-clicked card, or the focused element when a keyboard shortcut opens it.
To open at a point instead (the pointer position, or the caret for an `@`-mention picker), anchor positioning still
needs an element, so use a placeholder: an empty, zero-size `position: fixed` element kept directly before the menu,
moved to the point with `left` and `top` on each open, and passed as `source`. A zero-size anchor puts the menu's corner
at the point, as a native context menu does, and the flip fallbacks below still apply. Name the menu with `aria-label`
instead of `aria-labelledby`. Everything else in this guide applies unchanged; where it says "trigger" for positioning,
read the placeholder.

```html
<!-- Command invoker: the browser toggles the popover on click, Enter, and Space -->
<button id="actions-trigger" class="trigger" type="button" aria-haspopup="menu" aria-expanded="false"
  commandfor="actions-menu" command="toggle-popover">
  Actions
</button>
<!-- Immediately after its trigger, so browsers add no implicit aria-details -->
<div id="actions-menu" popover="auto">
  <!-- Nested, not on the popover: Chromium otherwise drops focusgroup keyboard behavior -->
  <div focusgroup="menu nomemory" aria-labelledby="actions-trigger">
    <button type="button">Duplicate</button>
    <button type="button">Rename</button>
    <button id="export-trigger" type="button" aria-haspopup="menu" aria-expanded="false"
      commandfor="export-menu" command="toggle-popover">
      Export <span aria-hidden="true">›</span>
    </button>
    <!-- Submenu: popover="auto" directly after its trigger, inside the parent focusgroup -->
    <div id="export-menu" popover="auto">
      <div focusgroup="menu nomemory" aria-labelledby="export-trigger">
        <button type="button">PDF</button>
        <button type="button">Plain Text</button>
      </div>
    </div>
  </div>
</div>
```

Name each menu with `aria-labelledby` pointing at its trigger. Keep decorative submenu indicators in CSS, or add
`aria-hidden="true"`. Give triggers with `aria-expanded="true"` a visible active style so users can tell which menu is
open. Outside a menu bar, style each trigger as a standalone button: it is its own `Tab` stop, and the styling must say
so. Anything that links triggers (`role="menubar"`, arrow keys between them, preview on focus) belongs to the
application menu bar.

### Position the menu with CSS Anchor Positioning

Use CSS anchor positioning, not JavaScript coordinates. Both `command="toggle-popover"` and
`showPopover({ source: trigger })` set an implicit anchor, so do not add per-menu `anchor-name` or `position-anchor`
rules. Menu behavior must not depend on anchor positioning.

```css
/* Top-level menus sit below their trigger, flipping when they would overflow. The implicit anchor comes from the invoker or source. */
[popover]:has(> [focusgroup~="menu"]) {
  position-area: block-end span-inline-end;
  position-try-fallbacks: flip-block, flip-inline, flip-block flip-inline;
  inset: auto;
}

/* A popover directly inside a menu is a submenu: beside its parent item, flipping when it would overflow. */
[focusgroup~="menu"] > [popover] {
  position-area: inline-end span-block-end;
  position-try-fallbacks: flip-inline, flip-block, --below;
}

/* Last resort for narrow viewports: directly below the trigger, indented, so the submenu never
   covers its trigger. */
@position-try --below {
  position-area: block-end span-inline-end;
  margin-inline-start: 1rem;
  /* Fit the area: the submenu's minimum width must not stop this fallback from fitting. */
  min-inline-size: 0;
  max-inline-size: calc(100% - 1rem);
}
```

Keep `--below` last so it applies only when neither side fits. It opens directly under the trigger, so on a narrow
screen it covers the sibling items beneath the trigger; that is the accepted trade-off for staying next to the trigger.
Also let the submenu shrink to the area (`min-inline-size: 0`, `max-inline-size` minus the indent). A fallback that does
not fit is skipped, and if none fit the browser keeps the base placement, so a submenu that is a few pixels too wide
silently covers its trigger.

For how the flip fallbacks work on a plain popover, see `viewport-aware-dropdowns` (via
`npx -y modern-web-guidance@latest retrieve "viewport-aware-dropdowns"`). That guide positions a button group, not a
menu; for menus, the submenu placement and `--below` fallback above take precedence.

### Animate open and close

Optional. Under 150 ms, `opacity` and a small `translate` only, same for submenus, inside
`@media (prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference)`. Focus moves on `toggle`, so the transition never delays keyboard
users.

```css
@media (prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference) {
  /* Closing: this rule is in effect once :popover-open is removed. */
  [popover]:has(> [focusgroup~="menu"]) {
    opacity: 0;
    translate: 0 -.25rem;
    transition: opacity, translate, display, overlay;
    transition-duration: .15s;
    /* Separate after transition so the shorthand doesn't reset it or fail in older browsers */
    transition-behavior: allow-discrete;
  }
  /* Opening: faster. */
  [popover]:has(> [focusgroup~="menu"]):popover-open {
    opacity: 1;
    translate: 0 0;
    transition-duration: .1s;
    @starting-style { opacity: 0; translate: 0 -.25rem; }
  }
}
```

`@starting-style` is not a repeat of `[popover]`: a closed popover is `display: none`, and transitions do not run from
an unrendered state, so it supplies the before-values for the open. Without it the open snaps and only the close
animates. `display` and `overlay` with `transition-behavior: allow-discrete` (set as a separate declaration after
`transition` so older browsers do not ignore the entire `transition` declaration) keep the popover rendered and in the
top layer until the close transition ends.

## Keyboard and focus

Do not add a second roving-tabindex system inside a focusgroup. Script covers only what the invokers and focusgroup do
not:

* **The trigger is an ordinary button.** `Tab` reaches it like any other button, and focusing it does not open the menu.
  `Enter`, `Space`, and click toggle the menu natively, so the script must not intercept these keys.
* **Keyboard open enters the menu.** Opening with `Enter` or `Space` focuses the first enabled item. `ArrowDown` on a
  trigger opens its menu if it is closed and focuses the first item either way, so arrow keys also work after a pointer
  open.
* **Pointer click on a closed trigger.** Opens it natively. Focus stays on the trigger; no item is focused. Only
  keyboard opens enter the menu.
* **Pointer click on an open trigger.** Closes it natively; it does not enter the menu.
    * **Known difference on submenu triggers.** A pointer click on a submenu trigger also toggles natively, so it can
      close a submenu that hover already previewed, or open one that has not appeared yet. Native menus only open it and
      never close it. This is harmless, so the guide accepts it.
* **Pointer over an item.** Focuses it without a ring, so hover and focus are one item.
* **Within a menu.** `ArrowUp` and `ArrowDown` move between enabled items. `Home` and `End` move to the first and last
  enabled item, which the script handles.
* **Submenu preview.** Focusing a submenu trigger, by arrow key or by pointer (which focuses it after a short delay),
  shows its submenu and sets `aria-expanded="true"`. Focus stays on the trigger, and no submenu item is focused. Moving
  to a sibling item closes the preview.
* **Enter or Space on a previewed submenu trigger.** They close the preview and keep focus on the trigger. The native
  `toggle-popover` action handles this.
* **ArrowRight on a submenu trigger.** Opens the submenu if needed and focuses its first item.
* **ArrowLeft or Escape in a submenu.** Closes only that submenu and restores focus to its trigger. The parent menu
  stays open.
* **Escape in a top-level menu.** Closes it and restores focus to its trigger.
* **Enter or Space on a command.** Activates it and closes all open menus.
* **Tab.** Leaves the menu system. Do not trap focus or step through every command. Closing must not leave focus inside
  hidden content.
* **No trigger button.** A menu opened from script focuses its first item when it was opened from the keyboard, and on
  close restores focus to the element that had it before the menu opened.

The `command` event fires before `toggle-popover` opens the menu, so focus cannot move into the menu there. Move focus
in the `toggle` event instead. HTML restores focus only for the first `popover="auto"` in a stack, so nested levels must
restore focus to their trigger explicitly.

## Implementing the interaction

Implement the behaviors above for your own markup. Arrow, `Home`/`End`, wrap-around and `Tab`-to-exit handling is
ordinary `keydown` code. A few parts are easy to get wrong, grouped below by input type.

### Keyboard and focus handling

1. **One open path.** Opening by keyboard calls `trigger.click()`, so the invoker's `toggle-popover` is the only way a
   menu opens. Mark the menu so the `toggle` handler enters it, keyboard opens only. On a pointer open, `toggle` focuses
   the trigger without a ring instead, because `pointerdown` prevented focus and arrow keys must still work.
2. **Submenu preview on focus.** Focusing a submenu trigger calls `showPopover({ source: trigger })` so the submenu
   anchors to it. Ignore focus returning from inside the trigger's own submenu (after `Escape`), or from another
   window (flag on window `blur`, cleared a tick after window `focus`). Hide a previewed submenu on `blur` unless focus
   moved into it. Top-level triggers get no preview: focusing them does nothing.
3. **Move focus in `toggle`, not `command`.** `command` fires before the menu opens.
4. **Restore focus to the trigger yourself.** Focus the trigger before `hidePopover()`. After a pointer activation,
   restore focus without a ring (`focus({ focusVisible: false })`), or the trigger shows the keyboard focus outline
   after a mouse click; keyboard activations keep the ring. A click with `event.detail === 0` came from the keyboard.
5. **Close one level at a time.** Call `stopPropagation()` on `Escape` and `ArrowLeft` in a submenu, or the parent's
   listener closes it too.

### Pointer handling

1. **Pointer click toggles.** Call `preventDefault()` on `pointerdown` so the click doesn't move focus. Remember which
   trigger was pressed. Clicking a closed trigger opens it natively and never enters the menu; only keyboard opens enter
   it. Do not intercept the click.
2. **Hover follows focus.** Style `:hover` and `:focus-visible` separately. On `pointermove` over an item, call
   `focus({ focusVisible: false })`; browsers that ignore the option paint no ring for pointer focus anyway. Pointer
   focus on a submenu trigger runs the same submenu preview as keyboard focus, after a short delay so a pointer crossing
   the item does not flash its submenu.
3. **Safe triangle.** A static CSS bridge is too narrow: it only works when the pointer starts near the parent's edge.
   Let CSS draw a triangle from where the pointer left the trigger, and use script only to place it:
    * Run this only when `matchMedia('(hover: hover)').matches`; it is irrelevant to touch and keyboard.
    * Start on `pointerleave` of a submenu trigger whose submenu is open, at the event's position. Skip a `--below`
      submenu, which has no side edge.
    * Set `--pointer-x` and `--pointer-y` (the pointer, in px relative to the submenu's box) on the submenu, and
      `data-bridge` to switch the bridge on. CSS derives the rest: which side the pointer is on from the sign of
      `--pointer-x`, and the submenu's near-edge corners from percentages of the pseudo-element's own box.
    * Pointer moves over the bridge target the submenu, so listen there: keep the bridge while the pointer moves toward
      the submenu, and remove the attribute about 300 ms after it rests, when it moves away from the submenu
      horizontally, when it reaches an item in the submenu, or when the submenu closes. A fixed 300 ms from the leave is
      too short for an unhurried diagonal; a bridge that ignores a reversal makes a change of mind wait.
    * CSS gives the submenu a `::before` clipped to a triangle from that point to the near-edge corners, with a few px
      of slack around the point (`--bridge-slack` below) so the pointer's own position is inside the shape rather than
      on its edge. The apex does not follow the pointer: an apex at the pointer turns every move into a direction test,
      and the first step off a straight line closes the submenu. It sits over the sibling items on the pointer's path,
      so they never receive the hover that would close the submenu. `clip-path` also limits hit testing, so the rest of
      the parent menu stays interactive.
    * The submenu needs `overflow: visible` (a popover clips by default). The pseudo-element extends `100vw`/`100vh`
      past it on every side, so the shape's points are offset by that, and `100%` of its box is the submenu plus twice
      that.
    * Follow-up: a curved path (`shape()` curve commands) follows real pointer arcs better than a straight triangle.

```css
[focusgroup~="menu"] > [popover] {
  overflow: visible;

  &[data-bridge]::before {
    content: "";
    position: absolute;
    inset: -100vh -100vw; /* Room for the triangle. In this box the submenu runs from 100vw/100vh to 100% - 100vw/100vh. */
    --bridge-slack: 5px; /* The apex moves away from the submenu by this much and is twice this tall. */
    --bridge-side: sign(var(--pointer-x)); /* -1: pointer left of the submenu, 1: right. */
    --bridge-edge: calc(50% + var(--bridge-side) * (50% - 100vw)); /* The submenu's near edge. */
    --bridge-apex: calc(100vw + var(--pointer-x) + var(--bridge-side) * var(--bridge-slack));
    clip-path: polygon(
      var(--bridge-apex) calc(100vh + var(--pointer-y) - var(--bridge-slack)),
      var(--bridge-edge) 100vh,
      var(--bridge-edge) calc(100% - 100vh),
      var(--bridge-apex) calc(100vh + var(--pointer-y) + var(--bridge-slack))
    );
  }
}
```

```js
const canHover = matchMedia('(hover: hover)');

// Call on pointerleave of a submenu trigger, with its submenu.
function startBridge(submenu, event) {
  if (!canHover.matches || !submenu.matches(':popover-open')) return;
  const rect = submenu.getBoundingClientRect();
  const left = event.clientX < rect.left;
  if (!left && event.clientX <= rect.right) return; // --below: no side edge.
  submenu.style.setProperty('--pointer-x', `${event.clientX - rect.left}px`);
  submenu.style.setProperty('--pointer-y', `${event.clientY - rect.top}px`);
  submenu.dataset.bridge = '';
  let timer;
  let lastX = event.clientX;
  const stop = () => {
    clearTimeout(timer);
    submenu.removeEventListener('pointermove', extend);
    submenu.removeAttribute('data-bridge');
  };
  const extend = ({ target, clientX }) => {
    // Reached an item, or turned away from the submenu.
    if (target !== submenu || (left ? clientX < lastX : clientX > lastX)) return stop();
    lastX = clientX;
    clearTimeout(timer);
    timer = setTimeout(stop, 300);
  };
  timer = setTimeout(stop, 300);
  submenu.addEventListener('pointermove', extend);
  submenu.addEventListener('toggle', stop, { once: true });
}
```

Hover follows focus (item 2) needs one guard. The move that leaves the trigger was hit-tested before the bridge existed,
so its target is the sibling under the pointer. Skip the focus when
`document.elementFromPoint(event.clientX, event.clientY)` is not inside the item; later moves on the path hit the
bridge, whose target is the submenu, not an item.

Also:

* **Outside focus.** Close every open menu when focus lands outside the menu system (a `document` `focusin` listener).
* **Command activation.** Announce it, then hide the root menu and restore focus to its trigger, without a ring if the
  activation came from a pointer. For checkable items (`menuitemcheckbox`, `menuitemradio`), wait about 300 ms before
  closing so the changed check mark is visible. Style a closed trigger as active only on `:focus-visible`; otherwise the
  restored (ringless) focus leaves it highlighted after a pointer selection.
* **`aria-expanded`.** Set it only in the `toggle` listener. It covers preview and open states, and a trigger's
  `aria-expanded` stays `"true"` while its menu is previewed or open.
* **Helpers.** The fallbacks below assume helpers you define for your markup: `triggers` (all `[commandfor]` buttons),
  `menuFor(trigger)`, `isOpen(menu)`, `closeAndRestore(menu, { fromPointer })` (focus the trigger, without a ring when
  `fromPointer`, then `menu.hidePopover()`), `enterOnOpen` (a `WeakSet` of menus to enter once open) and
  `pointerTrigger` (the trigger last pressed by a pointer).

### Submenus

* Use `popover="auto"` for submenus, placed after the submenu trigger inside the parent's `focusgroup`. Never
  `popover="manual"`.
* Nesting lets the browser keep the parent open, close sibling submenus, close child submenus when the root menu closes,
  and handle outside-click light dismiss.
* The submenu trigger keeps `aria-haspopup="menu"` and `aria-expanded`; the `toggle` listener keeps `aria-expanded` in
  sync.
* The keyboard script handles nested `Escape` and `ArrowLeft` as described above.
* A submenu trigger never also runs a command: one control cannot both activate and open, and `Enter` cannot mean both.
  Put the default action as the first submenu item, or add a separate command item beside the trigger. If a combined
  control is forced, document it as an accessibility tradeoff.

### Separators and checkable items

* Separate item groups with `<hr>` inside the focusgroup: a native `separator`, not focusable, skipped by focusgroup and
  the fallback. Never a styled `<div>`.
* A boolean option is a `<button type="button">` with `aria-checked` and an explicit `role="menuitemcheckbox"`.
  Focusgroup does not infer these roles, so this is the one place shared markup sets an item role.
* One of a set is a `<button type="button">` with `role="menuitemradio"` and `aria-checked`, inside a `role="group"`
  with an `aria-label`, in the same focusgroup.
* Script toggles `aria-checked`.
* `Enter` on a checkbox toggles and closes the menu; `Space` toggles and stays open (APG). Radios close on either key.
* Render the check mark from `[aria-checked="true"]::before`, not a separate icon element (see the CSS below).

### Not covered here

* **Activation feedback.** Native menus flash the chosen item before closing. If wanted, show a ~100 ms visual confirm
  before `hidePopover()`; do not delay focus restoration or the announcement.
* **Typeahead.** Focusgroup has none. If needed, on printable `keydown` match the current level's enabled item labels
  and focus the next match after the current item, wrapping. Do not intercept `Space`.

## Verify before finishing

An instruction cannot guarantee behavior, so test the result. Open the page and check each of these with the real
keyboard and mouse; fix and re-test any that fail:

* **Keyboard.** `Tab` lands on a trigger without opening its menu; `ArrowDown` opens and enters; `Escape` closes one
  level and returns focus to its trigger; `Tab` closes every menu.
* **Pointer open.** Clicking a trigger opens its menu with focus on the trigger and no ring; `ArrowDown` then enters;
  clicking again closes it.
* **Pointer command.** Clicking a command closes every menu and shows no focus ring on the trigger.
* **Submenu.** Moving diagonally from the middle of a submenu trigger to a submenu item keeps it open; moving to an
  unrelated sibling closes it.
* **Narrow screen.** At 375 px no submenu covers its own trigger.
* **Check marks.** Checked items show a check mark.
* **No leftovers.** No console errors, and no `popovertarget`, `popovertargetaction` or `aria-details` on triggers.

## Align menu item content

When a row has an icon, label, and shortcut or submenu indicator, reserve a fixed-size leading slot for the icon or
check mark and push the trailing content to the inline end. Icons are a known size, so a fixed slot keeps labels aligned
whether or not an item has an icon. Do not use `subgrid` for rows: any extra inline child (a badge, for example) becomes
its own grid item and breaks the layout. Hide shortcut text from assistive technology when it only repeats a key that
already operates the item.

```css
[focusgroup~="menu"] {
  --menu-icon-size: 1.25rem;
}

/* Target items only. A closed submenu popover inside the focusgroup must keep display: none. */
[focusgroup~="menu"] > button,
[focusgroup~="menu"] > [role="group"] > button {
  display: flex;
  align-items: center;
  gap: .5rem;
}

/* The leading slot holds the icon or check mark. */
[focusgroup~="menu"] button::before {
  content: "";
  flex: none;
  inline-size: var(--menu-icon-size);
}

/* Check mark for checked items. This selector must be at least as specific as the base
   ::before rule above, or the empty content wins and the check mark never shows. */
[focusgroup~="menu"] button[aria-checked="true"]::before {
  content: "✓";
}

/* Shortcut or submenu indicator at the inline end. */
[focusgroup~="menu"] .hint {
  margin-inline-start: auto;
}
```

Put a trailing indicator or shortcut in a `<span class="hint" aria-hidden="true">` inside the button; the submenu
trigger already announces its popup.

## Fallback strategies

### Fallbacks & browser support for focusgroup

Browser support for focusgroup: Limited availability.
Supported by: Chrome 150 (Jun 2026) and Edge 150 (Jul 2026).
Unsupported in: Firefox and Safari.

Keep `focusgroup="menu nomemory"` in the markup. If `'focusGroup' in HTMLElement.prototype` is false, install Up, Down,
Home, and End, set `role="menu"` on each menu container, and `role="menuitem"` on buttons with no role; leave checkable
items, `<hr>`, and `role="group"` alone. Never install it when native focusgroup is present. Submenu preview, open, and
close are author script either way.

```js
if (!('focusGroup' in HTMLElement.prototype)) {
  document.querySelectorAll('[focusgroup~="menu"]').forEach(group => {
    group.setAttribute('role', 'menu');
    group.querySelectorAll('button:not([role])').forEach(item => {
      item.setAttribute('role', 'menuitem');
    });
    group.addEventListener('keydown', event => {
      if (!['ArrowDown', 'ArrowUp', 'Home', 'End'].includes(event.key)) return;
      // Own items only: a nested submenu has its own focusgroup, a role="group" wrapper does not.
      const items = [...group.querySelectorAll('button')]
        .filter(item => item.closest('[focusgroup]') === group)
        .filter(item => !item.disabled && item.getAttribute('aria-disabled') !== 'true');
      const current = items.indexOf(document.activeElement);
      if (current < 0) return;
      const next = event.key === 'Home' ? 0 : event.key === 'End' ? items.length - 1 :
        (current + (event.key === 'ArrowUp' ? -1 : 1) + items.length) % items.length;
      event.preventDefault();
      event.stopImmediatePropagation();
      items[next].focus({ preventScroll: true });
    }, true);
  });
}
```

### Fallbacks & browser support for Popover

Baseline status for Popover: Newly available. It's been Baseline since 2025-01-27.
Supported by: Chrome 116 (Aug 2023), Edge 116 (Aug 2023), Firefox 125 (Apr 2024), Safari 17 (Sep 2023), and Safari iOS
18.3 (Jan 2025).

The Popover API is mostly **progressive enhancement**, but its defining behaviors — top-layer promotion, light-dismiss,
and `popovertarget` invocation — have no CSS-only equivalent. Older browsers need a polyfill, or a manual fallback if
you would rather not ship one.

**Polyfill:** To support the `popover` attribute in older browsers, conditionally load [
`@oddbird/popover-polyfill`](https://github.com/oddbird/popover-polyfill). **MANDATORY:** Feature detect by checking for
the `popover` property on `HTMLElement.prototype`, and load the polyfill **only** when native support is missing — do
NOT load it unconditionally.

With a bundler or import map:

```js
// MANDATORY: Feature detect 'popover' on HTMLElement.prototype.
if (!Object.hasOwn(HTMLElement.prototype, "popover")) {
  import("@oddbird/popover-polyfill");
}
```

If not using a package manager, import from a CDN, e.g.
`"https://unpkg.com/@oddbird/popover-polyfill@latest/dist/popover.min.js"`.

Caveats when using the polyfill:

- Do NOT use the `popover` IDL attribute for any code that may run before the polyfill is fully loaded. It will not be
  mirrored as an attribute, the popover will not be picked up by the polyfill, and the property will be shadowing the
  accessor the polyfill adds forever. Use `setAttribute()`/`removeAttribute()` instead.
- **Styling caveat:** The polyfill cannot define the real `:popover-open` pseudo-class, so it applies a
  `.\:popover-open` class instead. **MANDATORY:** Combine the two with `:is()` or `:where()`, otherwise browsers that
  lack `:popover-open` discard the entire rule:

```css
[popover]:is(:popover-open, .\:popover-open) {
  display: block;
}
```

### Fallbacks & browser support for Anchor positioning

Browser support for Anchor positioning: Limited availability.
Supported by: Chrome 157 (Nov 2026), Edge 157 (Nov 2026), and Safari 27 (Sep 2026).
Unsupported in: Firefox.

Without CSS Anchor Positioning, a popover falls back to the UA's centered viewport placement. Never ship that for a
menu: it detaches the menu from its trigger, and a centered submenu covers its parent. Gate the anchored rules behind
`@supports (position-area: block-end)` and position the menu from script when it fails:

* Place the menu below its trigger (top level) or beside it (submenu), flipping to the other side and clamping to the
  viewport when it would overflow.
* Run it in the `toggle` handler when the menu opens, and apply the result as `left` and `top` on the menu. Use
  `position: fixed` with `inset: auto` and `margin: 0` so the coordinates are viewport-relative.
* Keep these overrides inside `@supports not (position-area: block-end)`, so browsers with anchor positioning are
  unaffected.

Baseline status for the api.HTMLElement.showPopover.options_source_parameter.implicit_anchor_reference capability: Newly
available. It's been Baseline since 2026-01-13.
Supported by: Chrome 137 (May 2025), Edge 137 (May 2025), Firefox 147 (Jan 2026), and Safari 26 (Sep 2025).

If targeting earlier implementations where `showPopover({ source })` does not establish an implicit anchor (no `source`
on `ToggleEvent.prototype`), give each trigger a unique `anchor-name` and each menu a matching `position-anchor` from
script, instead of writing per-menu CSS rules.

For browsers without anchor positioning at all, see `viewport-aware-dropdowns` (via
`npx -y modern-web-guidance@latest retrieve "viewport-aware-dropdowns"`) for the polyfill route.

### Fallbacks & browser support for Invoker commands

Baseline status for Invoker commands: Newly available. It's been Baseline since 2025-12-12.
Supported by: Chrome 135 (Apr 2025), Edge 135 (Apr 2025), Firefox 144 (Oct 2025), and Safari 26.2 (Dec 2025).

Without invokers, `command="toggle-popover"` does nothing, so script must toggle the menu.

* Feature-detect the interface, not an instance: `'commandForElement' in HTMLButtonElement.prototype`.
* On each trigger `click`, call `preventDefault()` so a browser with invokers cannot toggle twice.
* If the menu is open, close it with `closeAndRestore(menu)`. Otherwise call `menu.showPopover({ source: trigger })`.
* Mark the menu in `enterOnOpen` unless the click came from the pressed trigger (`pointerTrigger`), so only keyboard
  opens enter the menu.
* `Enter` and `Space` still work because they generate a click on buttons.

### Fallbacks & browser support for `:has()`

Baseline status for :has(): Widely available. It's been Baseline since 2023-12-19.
Supported by: Chrome 105 (Sep 2022), Edge 105 (Sep 2022), Firefox 121 (Dec 2023), and Safari 15.4 (Mar 2022).

If targeting browsers without `:has()`, add a class to each menu popover instead of selecting
`[popover]:has(> [focusgroup~="menu"])`.

### Fallbacks & browser support for `sign()`

Baseline status for abs() and sign(): Newly available. It's been Baseline since 2025-06-26.
Supported by: Chrome 138 (Jun 2025), Edge 138 (Jun 2025), Firefox 118 (Sep 2023), and Safari 15.4 (Mar 2022).

If your Baseline target lacks `sign()`, skip `--bridge-side` and pick the edge and the apex nudge with `clamp()`: a
large multiplier pushes `--pointer-x` past either bound, so the result is one end or the other.

```css
@supports not (width: calc(sign(1px) * 1px)) {
  [data-bridge]::before {
    --bridge-edge: clamp(100vw, 50% + var(--pointer-x) * 1e6, 100% - 100vw);
    --bridge-apex: calc(100vw + var(--pointer-x) + clamp(-1 * var(--bridge-slack), var(--pointer-x) * 1e6, var(--bridge-slack)));
  }
}
```

# Responsive Site Navigation

Build a site navigation bar that uses one semantic navigation tree at every size, presents a native popover when the
links do not fit, becomes an inline navigation when they do, and identifies the current page.

This guide describes site-navigation integration. It is navigation, not an application menu: links stay in the `Tab`
order, with no `focusgroup`, `role="menubar"`, `role="menu"`, `role="menuitem"`, `aria-haspopup="menu"`, or arrow-key
handling. For application command menus, see `menu` (via `npx -y modern-web-guidance@latest retrieve "menu"`); for
menubars, see `app-menus` (via `npx -y modern-web-guidance@latest retrieve "app-menus"`). For the menu and chevron
icons, see `icons` (via `npx -y modern-web-guidance@latest retrieve "icons"`).

For component-driven layouts, fluid sizing, and typographic line-wrapping, see `size-aware-styling` (via
`npx -y modern-web-guidance@latest retrieve "size-aware-styling"`), `fluid-scaling` (via
`npx -y modern-web-guidance@latest retrieve "fluid-scaling"`), and `improve-text-layout-and-legibility` (via
`npx -y modern-web-guidance@latest retrieve "improve-text-layout-and-legibility"`).

## Core Markup

Use one `<nav>` landmark for narrow and wide layouts. Wrap it in a semantic `<header>` whose `is-wide` class selects the
inline layout. The collapsed layout is the default, so it is also what you get without script.

```html
<header class="site-header">
  <div class="header-inner">
    <a class="site-logo" href="index.html">Acme</a>

    <nav class="site-nav" aria-label="Primary">
      <button
        class="menu-button"
        type="button"
        popovertarget="site-menu"
        popovertargetaction="toggle"
        aria-controls="site-menu"
      >
        <!-- Decorative menu icon: insert as described in the icons guide -->
        <span>Menu</span>
      </button>

      <ul id="site-menu" class="site-menu" popover="auto">
        <li><a href="index.html" aria-current="page">Home</a></li>
        <li><a href="about.html">About</a></li>
        <li class="nav-dropdown">
          <button
            class="dropdown-trigger"
            type="button"
            aria-expanded="false"
            aria-controls="services-menu"
            popovertarget="services-menu"
          >
            Services
          </button>
          <ul id="services-menu" class="dropdown-list">
            <li><a href="design.html">Design</a></li>
            <li><a href="development.html">Development</a></li>
          </ul>
        </li>
      </ul>
    </nav>
  </div>
</header>
```

The button declaratively controls the menu with `popovertarget` and `aria-controls`. The `nav` remains the navigation
landmark while the menu is closed. The trigger icon is decorative and the visible "Menu" text is the accessible name, so
hide the icon from assistive technologies. For how to insert and hide icons, see `icons` (via
`npx -y modern-web-guidance@latest retrieve "icons"`). For the general popover control contract, see
`declarative-dialog-popover-control` (via
`npx -y modern-web-guidance@latest retrieve "declarative-dialog-popover-control"`). Unlike the menu guide, use
`popovertarget`: one toggle needs no invoker commands. As in the menu guide, place each popover (the menu list, and the
submenu list) immediately after its trigger so browsers add no implicit `aria-details`.

## Narrow Layout: Popover Navigation

When collapsed, keep `popover="auto"` on the navigation list. Anchor the fixed popover to the menu button and constrain
its height so a long navigation can scroll without exceeding the viewport.

There is no hard-coded breakpoint. Script collapses the navigation only when the inline row (brand, actions and every
link) does not fit, so adding a link, a translation or larger text moves the point automatically. It adds `is-wide` to
the header when the row fits; without script the header keeps the collapsed layout at every width.

```css
/* Keep the row's natural width measurable */
.header-inner > * {
  flex-shrink: 0;
  white-space: nowrap;
}

.site-header {
  .menu-button {
    anchor-name: --menu-button;
  }

  .site-menu {
    position: fixed;
    inset: auto;
    inset-block-start: anchor(--menu-button bottom);
    inset-inline-end: 1rem;
    inline-size: min(80dvw, 24rem);
    max-inline-size: calc(100dvw - 2rem);
    block-size: fit-content;
    max-block-size: calc(100dvh - 6rem);
    margin-block-start: 0.5rem;
    overflow: auto;
  }
}
```

The `anchor()` declaration places the menu below the button; see Fallbacks for browsers without Anchor Positioning. For
collision-aware positioning near viewport edges, see `viewport-aware-dropdowns` (via
`npx -y modern-web-guidance@latest retrieve "viewport-aware-dropdowns"`).

## Wide Layout: Inline Navigation

When the row fits, hide the collapsed-layout trigger and reset the popover presentation so the same list participates in
the header as an inline navigation.

```css
.site-header.is-wide {
  .menu-button {
    display: none;
  }

  .site-menu {
    position: static;
    display: flex;
    align-items: center;
    gap: 0.25rem;
    inline-size: auto;
    max-inline-size: none;
    block-size: auto;
    max-block-size: none;
    overflow: visible;
    margin: 0;
    padding: 0;
    border: 0;
    background: transparent;
    box-shadow: none;
  }

  .site-menu::backdrop {
    display: none;
  }
}
```

CSS changes the presentation, but JavaScript decides which layout applies and must also synchronize the `popover`
attribute with it. Measure the inline row: show it inline, compare `scrollWidth` with `clientWidth` on the header's
inner row, then toggle `is-wide`. Add a temporary `is-measuring` class that sets `transition: none` on descendants for
the measurement and remove it in `requestAnimationFrame`, otherwise the menu animates from its inline styles on every
resize and flickers. Keep the navigation as a popover only in the collapsed layout; remove the attribute in the inline
layout. Removing it closes an open popover, so note whether the menu was open and call `showPopover()` again if the
layout is still collapsed; otherwise a resize closes the open menu. Run one shared function from `ResizeObserver`s on
the header and the navigation list, so font loading and text changes are caught without special cases. Remeasure while
inline on every notification, but while collapsed only when the header's width has grown. Switching to inline just to
measure on every shrink makes the layout thrash. The tradeoff is that a collapsed menu that gets smaller by itself (for
example a shorter translation) stays collapsed until the header grows. Do not infer the layout from a hidden trigger.

## Nested Site Navigation

Use a `<button>` with `aria-expanded` and `aria-controls` as the trigger for nested site navigation, followed
immediately by the submenu list. DO NOT use `<details>` and `<summary>`: `<summary>` should map to a `button` role, but
has not been consistently implemented in browsers, so screen readers announce it inconsistently (for example as "
summary" or "disclosure triangle").

One list must be an inline disclosure when narrow and a floating popover when wide. A top-layer popover cannot render in
flow, so `popover` is set only in the wide layout, where `popovertarget` opens it natively. Leave `popover` off the
submenu in the markup: without script it stays a nested list inside the menu, matching the narrow layout. In the narrow
layout a small click handler toggles `hidden` and `aria-expanded`. Hide the narrow submenu from script, not in the
markup.

Synchronize the layout state from the same function that handles the navigation list. When inline, set `popover="auto"`
on the submenu, clear `hidden`, and let the native `toggle` event drive `aria-expanded`. When narrow, remove `popover`,
set `hidden` from script, and let a click handler toggle `hidden` and `aria-expanded`:

```js
const wide = inner.scrollWidth <= inner.clientWidth; // measured with is-wide set
if (wide) submenu.setAttribute("popover", "auto");
else submenu.removeAttribute("popover");
submenu.hidden = !wide;
trigger.setAttribute("aria-expanded", "false");
```

> [!NOTE]
> Use `setAttribute()`/`removeAttribute()`, NOT the `popover` JS property, as it can cause race conditions if popover is
> used through a polyfill.

Do not add document-level click-outside, Escape or focus-restoration handlers. The native popover provides those
interactions in the wide layout, and the narrow disclosure needs only the click handler. The declarative `popovertarget`
makes the button the submenu's implicit anchor, so wide-layout positioning can use `position-area` without a separate
`anchor-name` or `position-anchor` declaration.

### Hover preview

In the wide layout, open the submenu (`submenu.showPopover({ source: trigger })`) on `pointerenter` of the parent `<li>`
when `matchMedia("(hover: hover)").matches` and `event.pointerType !== "touch"`, and hide it on `pointerleave` if it is
still only hover-previewed (if the user clicks the trigger while previewing, clear the preview flag and call
`event.preventDefault()` so the click pins it open instead of toggling it closed). Do not open it when the trigger
receives keyboard focus; only `Enter` or `Space` toggles it. Close the open submenu when focus moves to an element
outside the submenu's whole list item (`focusout` with a non-null `relatedTarget` outside it), so tabbing or `Shift`+
`Tab`bing away closes it.

Position the wide submenu below its trigger with CSS Anchor Positioning (`position-area: block-end span-inline-end` and
`position-try-fallbacks: flip-block, flip-inline`). For collision-aware positioning of a plain popover, see
`viewport-aware-dropdowns` (via `npx -y modern-web-guidance@latest retrieve "viewport-aware-dropdowns"`). Add a
`::before` bridge across any margin gap above the submenu (with `overflow: visible` on the popover) so moving the
pointer from the trigger into the submenu does not fire `pointerleave`, and set `height: auto` to prevent Safari from
stretching the positioned popover to its placement area:

```css
.site-header.is-wide {
  .dropdown-list[popover] {
    position: absolute;
    position-area: block-end span-inline-end;
    position-try-fallbacks: flip-block, flip-inline;
    inset: auto;
    height: auto;
    inline-size: max-content;
    min-inline-size: 12rem;
    margin-block-start: 0.5rem;
    overflow: visible;
  }

  .dropdown-list::before {
    content: "";
    position: absolute;
    inset-inline: 0;
    inset-block-end: 100%;
    block-size: 0.5rem;
  }

  /* Also hides the list before script sets popover, so an open narrow disclosure cannot widen the measured row */
  .dropdown-list:not(:is(:popover-open, .\:popover-open)) {
    display: none;
  }

  .dropdown-list:is(:popover-open, .\:popover-open) {
    display: grid;
  }
}
```

## Indicating the Current Page

Use `aria-current="page"` to identify the current page. Set it at build time or with JavaScript, and use
`[aria-current="page"]` as the CSS styling hook. The visual treatment is a design decision; do not assume a particular
pseudo-element, border, or orientation. Do not indicate the current page with color alone (WCAG 1.4.1). Ensure the color
of the visual indicator has a contrast of at least `3:1` with the background color.

## Transitions and Accessibility

If the navigation is animated (optional; add it when the abrupt open and close feels out of place), use
`@starting-style`, include `display` and `overlay` in `transition`, and declare `transition-behavior: allow-discrete` as
a separate property after `transition` (DO NOT put `allow-discrete` in the `transition` shorthand, which makes older
browsers ignore the entire `transition` declaration) for both the mobile menu and the wide floating submenu. Animate
only `opacity` and `translate`, and respect `prefers-reduced-motion`. For the reusable transition pattern, see
`animate-element-entry-exit` (via `npx -y modern-web-guidance@latest retrieve "animate-element-entry-exit"`).

### Optional: Narrow submenu slide-down

Optional. In the narrow layout the submenu is an inline list toggled with `hidden`, which opens instantly by default and
is fully functional that way. To slide it open and closed:

- Keep the `[hidden]` list rendered with `display: grid` and `block-size: 0`, then transition `block-size` to `auto`
  with `interpolate-size: allow-keywords` and `clip-path: inset(-6px)` to clip the slide without cutting off the focus
  ring (not `overflow: clip`, which clips the ring; `6px` is an example, use at least the ring's outline width plus
  offset).
- Set `content-visibility: hidden` on the `[hidden]` list, include `content-visibility` in `transition`, and declare
  `transition-behavior: allow-discrete` separately after `transition` so the content stays rendered until the close
  finishes.
- Scope it to the collapsed layout and `prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference`; outside it, `[hidden]` must stay
  `display: none`. In the wide layout the submenu is a popover and must not be clipped.
- For the general technique, see `animate-to-intrinsic-sizes` (via
  `npx -y modern-web-guidance@latest retrieve "animate-to-intrinsic-sizes"`).

Use logical properties for sizing, spacing, and positioning. Use `dvw` and `dvh` for viewport-relative limits, provide
visible `:focus-visible` indicators, and adapt custom borders and current-page indicators under `forced-colors: active`.

## Fallbacks

### Fallbacks & browser support for Popover

Baseline status for Popover: Newly available. It's been Baseline since 2025-01-27.
Supported by: Chrome 116 (Aug 2023), Edge 116 (Aug 2023), Firefox 125 (Apr 2024), Safari 17 (Sep 2023), and Safari iOS
18.3 (Jan 2025).

The Popover API is mostly **progressive enhancement**, but its defining behaviors — top-layer promotion, light-dismiss,
and `popovertarget` invocation — have no CSS-only equivalent. Older browsers need a polyfill, or a manual fallback if
you would rather not ship one.

**Polyfill:** To support the `popover` attribute in older browsers, conditionally load [
`@oddbird/popover-polyfill`](https://github.com/oddbird/popover-polyfill). **MANDATORY:** Feature detect by checking for
the `popover` property on `HTMLElement.prototype`, and load the polyfill **only** when native support is missing — do
NOT load it unconditionally.

With a bundler or import map:

```js
// MANDATORY: Feature detect 'popover' on HTMLElement.prototype.
if (!Object.hasOwn(HTMLElement.prototype, "popover")) {
  import("@oddbird/popover-polyfill");
}
```

If not using a package manager, import from a CDN, e.g.
`"https://unpkg.com/@oddbird/popover-polyfill@latest/dist/popover.min.js"`.

Caveats when using the polyfill:

- Do NOT use the `popover` IDL attribute for any code that may run before the polyfill is fully loaded. It will not be
  mirrored as an attribute, the popover will not be picked up by the polyfill, and the property will be shadowing the
  accessor the polyfill adds forever. Use `setAttribute()`/`removeAttribute()` instead.
- **Styling caveat:** The polyfill cannot define the real `:popover-open` pseudo-class, so it applies a
  `.\:popover-open` class instead. **MANDATORY:** Combine the two with `:is()` or `:where()`, otherwise browsers that
  lack `:popover-open` discard the entire rule:

```css
[popover]:is(:popover-open, .\:popover-open) {
  display: block;
}
```

### Fallbacks & browser support for Anchor positioning

Browser support for Anchor positioning: Limited availability.
Supported by: Chrome 157 (Nov 2026), Edge 157 (Nov 2026), and Safari 27 (Sep 2026).
Unsupported in: Firefox.

For the mobile menu, put an absolute fallback declaration before the `anchor()` declaration. Do not wrap this simple
fallback in an `@supports` rule: an unsupported `anchor()` declaration is discarded while the preceding declaration
remains valid. Without Anchor Positioning the menu still opens as a popover at a fixed offset from the top of the
viewport.

```css
.site-header {
  .site-menu {
    /* Example-only offset: use roughly your header height. Browsers without anchor() keep this one. */
    inset-block-start: 4.75rem;
    inset-block-start: anchor(--menu-button bottom);
  }
}
```

For the wide floating submenu, without CSS Anchor Positioning a popover falls back to centered viewport placement, which
detaches the submenu from its navbar trigger. Override the submenu to `position: fixed; margin: 0` inside
`@supports not (position-area: block-end)`, and when
`event.newState === "open" && !CSS.supports("position-area", "block-end")` in the submenu's `toggle` handler, compute
`top` and `left` from `trigger.getBoundingClientRect()` and `submenu.getBoundingClientRect()` (placing it below the
trigger, flipping above if `top + size.height > innerHeight`, and clamping `left` to `[0, innerWidth - size.width]`).

### Transitions

Baseline status for @starting-style: Newly available. It's been Baseline since 2024-08-06.
Supported by: Chrome 117 (Sep 2023), Edge 117 (Sep 2023), Firefox 129 (Aug 2024), and Safari 17.5 (May 2024).

Baseline status for transition-behavior: Newly available. It's been Baseline since 2024-08-06.
Supported by: Chrome 117 (Sep 2023), Edge 117 (Sep 2023), Firefox 129 (Aug 2024), and Safari 17.4 (Mar 2024).

Browser support for interpolate-size: Limited availability.
Supported by: Chrome 129 (Sep 2024) and Edge 129 (Sep 2024).
Unsupported in: Firefox and Safari.

Baseline status for content-visibility: Newly available. It's been Baseline since 2025-09-15.
Supported by: Chrome 108 (Nov 2022), Edge 108 (Dec 2022), Firefox 130 (Sep 2024), and Safari 26 (Sep 2025).

Gate the optional narrow submenu slide-down rules that override `[hidden]` with `display: grid` behind
`@supports (interpolate-size: allow-keywords)`. Without the gate, browsers lacking keyword interpolation snap the list
closed instead of sliding; with it, they keep native `[hidden]` behavior. Without `@starting-style` or
`transition-behavior: allow-discrete`, the optional popover entry or exit transitions fall back to opening or closing
immediately.

Without script nothing adds `is-wide`, so the header stays collapsed: the menu button opens the native popover and the
submenu is a nested list. Do not write a separate no-script layout or a `no-js` class.

# Navigation Drawer

## Overview

A navigation drawer is a panel that slides in from the edge of the viewport over the page content, dimming everything
behind it. It is opened from a trigger button and dismissed by swiping the panel off-screen, tapping the dimmed
backdrop, activating an explicit Close button inside the panel, or pressing Escape.

This guide implements the drawer as:

- A top-layer element (a modal `<dialog>` or a `popover="manual"` element,
  see [Choose the drawer element](#choose-the-drawer-element)), so the panel and its `::backdrop` overlay every other
  element on the page, regardless of stacking context.
- A horizontally scrolling container with two CSS scroll-snap stops — one for "open", one for "closed" — so the swipe
  gesture is handled natively by the browser. This delivers momentum, velocity, and interruption tracking for free, with
  no JavaScript pointer-event code.
- A scroll-driven animation that ties the backdrop's opacity to the scroll position, so the dim fades in and out
  smoothly as the user drags the panel.
- An `IntersectionObserver` on the panel that detects when it has fully entered or fully left the viewport, and uses
  those moments to close the drawer and update its state.

This approach is preferred over JavaScript-driven `transform` animations because the scroll mechanism gives the user
direct control of the panel's position (their finger drives it, not a tween) and it much more closely matches the
interaction patterns that users are accustomed to in native mobile apps.

### Choose the drawer element

First, decide whether the drawer is only ever a drawer, or whether the same element also becomes a regular,
always-visible sidebar under certain conditions (e.g. on wide screens). If the request does not say, assume it is only
ever a drawer.

- **Only ever a drawer**: use a `<dialog>` element opened with `showModal()`. The browser makes the rest of the page
  inert, exposes the drawer as a modal dialog to assistive technologies, handles Escape, and restores focus on close.
  See [Implementation with `<dialog>`](#implementation-with-dialog).
- **Also a sidebar**: use a regular element with `role="dialog"` and `popover="manual"`, and remove the `role` while it
  acts as a sidebar. A `<dialog>` element does not work here, since it is always exposed as a dialog, but a sidebar is
  not one. Because a popover is not modal, the code must handle modality manually.
  See [Implementation for a drawer that also acts as a sidebar](#implementation-for-a-drawer-that-also-acts-as-a-sidebar).

## Implementation with `<dialog>`

### 1. Markup

The drawer is a single `<dialog>` containing a horizontal scroller, which contains the visible "sheet". The trigger
button lives in the page content. The drawer's close button has an `autofocus` attribute so that this control receives
focus when the drawer is opened.

```html
<!-- MANDATORY: Provide an accessible name for the dialog with aria-label or,
     if there is already text within the drawer that can act as its accessible name,
     with aria-labelledby. -->
<dialog class="Drawer" id="drawer" aria-label="Navigation drawer">
  <div class="Drawer-scroller">
    <nav class="Drawer-sheet">
      <!-- Close button that can be used to dismiss the drawer -->
      <button id="drawer-close" aria-label="Close menu" autofocus>
        <!-- close icon or blank if icon inserted via CSS -->
      </button>
      <ul>
        <li><a href="/page-1">Page 1</a></li>
        <li><a href="/page-2">Page 2</a></li>
        <!-- ... -->
      </ul>
    </nav>
  </div>
</dialog>

<main>
  <header>
    <!-- aria-controls links the trigger to the drawer; aria-expanded
         reflects the current state for assistive tech. -->
    <button id="drawer-open"
            aria-label="Menu"
            aria-expanded="false"
            aria-controls="drawer">
      <!-- open icon or blank if icon inserted via CSS -->
    </button>
  </header>
  <!-- Page content. -->
</main>
```

See `icons` (via `npx -y modern-web-guidance@latest retrieve "icons"`) for maintaining accessibility when using icons.

### 2. Styles

#### Reset the dialog and fill the viewport

The dialog must cover the whole viewport so that the swipe surface extends edge-to-edge. The default user-agent dialog
styles (centered, size-capped, padded, bordered) get in the way and must be reset.

```css
.Drawer {
  /* min() caps the sheet width on large screens but on a phone leaves
     a 20% peek of page content visible, which is the affordance that
     tells the user they can tap outside to dismiss. */
  --drawer-width: min(20em, 80dvw, 100dvw - 24px);

  /* Custom property driven by the scroll-driven animation below.
     0 = drawer fully closed (transparent backdrop).
     1 = drawer fully open (visible backdrop). */
  --drawer-backdrop: 0;

  /* Reset UA dialog styles that would constrain the element. */
  inset: 0;
  width: auto;
  height: auto;
  max-width: none;
  max-height: none;
  margin: 0;
  padding: 0;
  background: transparent;
  border: 0;
  overflow: visible;
}

/* Style the dialog's ::backdrop to achieve the overlay effect and
   provide visual affordances indicating that the rest of the page is inert */
.Drawer::backdrop {
  background: #000;
  /* Use calc() to limit the opacity range so the content beneath is visible */
  opacity: calc(var(--drawer-backdrop) / 2);
}
```

#### Build the swipe surface with scroll snap

The scroller is a horizontal grid wider than the viewport: column 1 holds the sheet (width `--drawer-width`), column 2
is an empty pseudo-element spacer the width of the viewport. Snapping between the two columns is what opens and closes
the drawer.

```css
.Drawer-scroller {
  position: relative;
  display: grid;
  /* Sheet on the left, full-viewport spacer on the right. The user
     scrolls between the two snap stops to open and close. */
  grid-template-columns: var(--drawer-width) 100%;

  overflow-x: scroll;
  /* Stop the swipe from chaining into the page's vertical scroll
     when the user reaches either snap edge. */
  overscroll-behavior: none;
  scrollbar-width: none;
  /* `mandatory` guarantees the drawer always settles fully open or
     fully closed — never half-open after a partial swipe. */
  scroll-snap-type: x mandatory;
}

/* Enable smooth scrolling natively, but only if the user has not
   requested reduced motion. */
@media (prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference) {
  .Drawer-scroller {
    scroll-behavior: smooth;
  }
}

/* The empty spacer that creates the "closed" snap stop. */
.Drawer-scroller::after {
  content: '';
  scroll-snap-align: end;
  /* Open the drawer already scrolled to this stop (drawer off-screen),
     so the JS only needs to scroll to the open position to
     animate it in. */
  scroll-initial-target: nearest;
}

.Drawer-sheet {
  display: grid;
  grid-template-rows: auto 1fr;
  /* Use `svh` (small viewport height) — not `vh` or `dvh` — so the
     sheet height does not jump when the iOS Safari address bar
     resizes mid-swipe. */
  height: 100svh;

  background: #333;
  color: #fff;
  overflow-y: auto;
  scroll-snap-align: start;
  scrollbar-width: none;
}
```

#### Tie the backdrop opacity to the scroll position

A scroll-driven animation maps `--drawer-backdrop` from 1 (open) to 0 (closed) across the scroller's range, so the
backdrop fades in and out perfectly synced with the drag.

```css
/* MANDATORY: Wrap this entire block in @supports. Browsers that don't
   support animation-timeline still parse the @keyframes and would
   apply the animation's `0%` value (--drawer-backdrop: 1) at all
   times, leaving the backdrop permanently opaque. The @supports gate
   ensures the animation is only registered where it actually works. */
@supports (animation-timeline: scroll()) {
  .Drawer {
    /* timeline-scope lets .Drawer reference a scroll-timeline that
       is defined on its descendant (the scroller). Without this, the
       timeline name is not visible to the .Drawer element. */
    timeline-scope: --drawer-fade;
    animation: fade-drawer-backdrop linear both;
    animation-timeline: --drawer-fade;
  }

  .Drawer-scroller {
    /* The horizontal scroll position of this element drives the
       timeline named `--drawer-fade`. */
    scroll-timeline: --drawer-fade x;
  }

  /* @property is REQUIRED. Without registering --drawer-backdrop with
     a `<number>` syntax, the browser treats it as a string and cannot
     interpolate it — the backdrop would jump from 0 to 1 with no
     fade. */
  @property --drawer-backdrop {
    syntax: '<number>';
    inherits: true;
    initial-value: 0;
  }

  @keyframes fade-drawer-backdrop {
    /* Scroll position 0 = drawer fully open = backdrop visible. */
    0% { --drawer-backdrop: 1 }
    /* Scroll position 100% = drawer fully closed = backdrop hidden. */
    100% { --drawer-backdrop: 0 }
  }
}
```

### 3. Open and close the drawer

Opening is two steps: show the dialog as modal, then scroll the sheet into view. Closing is one step: scroll back to the
spacer; an observer (step 4) closes the dialog once the sheet is fully off-screen.

```js
const drawer = document.getElementById('drawer');
const openBtn = document.getElementById('drawer-open');
const scroller = drawer.querySelector('.Drawer-scroller');
const sheet = drawer.querySelector('.Drawer-sheet');
const closeBtn = document.getElementById('drawer-close');

function openDrawer() {
  // Show the dialog first so the element is in the top layer before
  // we trigger any scrolling. `scroll-initial-target` (set on the
  // ::after spacer) places the initial scroll position at the closed
  // stop, so the drawer enters the top layer already off-screen.
  drawer.showModal();

  // Scroll the sheet into view. The `behavior: 'auto'` option defers
  // to the CSS `scroll-behavior` property, which will be smooth unless
  // the user prefers reduced motion. Snap takes over at the end and
  // locks the drawer fully open.
  scroller.scrollTo({left: 0, behavior: 'auto'});
}

function closeDrawer() {
  // Scroll back to the spacer. Do NOT call close() here —
  // doing so would remove the element from the top layer mid-animation
  // and the close animation would not be visible. The
  // IntersectionObserver in step 4 closes the dialog once the sheet
  // has actually left the viewport.
  scroller.scrollTo({left: scroller.offsetWidth, behavior: 'auto'});
}
```

### 4. Detect open and closed state

Use an `IntersectionObserver` on the sheet — not the scroll position — as the source of truth for the drawer's state.
The observer fires regardless of how the sheet moved (user swipe, programmatic scroll, snap settle), so all dismissal
paths converge in the same callback.

Because the drawer is a modal `<dialog>`, the browser makes the rest of the page inert while it is open and moves focus
back to the trigger button when it closes, so these callbacks only need to close the dialog and keep `aria-expanded` in
sync.

```js
function onDrawerOpened() {
  openBtn.setAttribute('aria-expanded', 'true');
}

function onDrawerClosed() {
  // Close the dialog only after the close animation completes,
  // so the slide-out is visible to the user.
  drawer.close();
  openBtn.setAttribute('aria-expanded', 'false');
}

// Treat "any pixel of the sheet visible inside the dialog" as
// "open enough to count as not closed". This threshold is intentionally
// tiny so the closed callback only fires once the sheet is truly gone.
const visibleThreshold = 1 / window.innerWidth;

const observer = new IntersectionObserver(
  (entries) => {
    // During programmatic scrolling the observer can deliver multiple
    // entries in one batch. Only the most recent describes the
    // current state; earlier entries are intermediate positions.
    const entry = entries.at(-1);
    if (entry.intersectionRatio < visibleThreshold) onDrawerClosed();
    if (entry.intersectionRatio === 1) onDrawerOpened();
  },
  // root: drawer makes the dialog element the intersection root,
  // so the ratio reflects the sheet's visibility within the dialog
  // (i.e. how much of it has been swiped on-screen).
  {root: drawer, threshold: [visibleThreshold, 1]},
);
observer.observe(sheet);
```

### 5. Wire up the trigger and dismissal handlers

```js
// Open trigger.
openBtn.addEventListener('click', openDrawer);

// Close trigger.
closeBtn.addEventListener('click', closeDrawer);

// Light-dismiss: a tap on the dimmed area (anywhere inside the
// dialog but outside the sheet) closes the drawer. Do not use
// closedby="any": the dialog fills the viewport, so taps land on the
// dialog rather than its ::backdrop, and it would close without the
// slide-out animation.
drawer.addEventListener('click', (event) => {
  if (!sheet.contains(event.target)) closeDrawer();
});

// Escape key. A modal dialog fires `cancel` on Escape; prevent the
// instant close and slide the drawer out instead.
// NOTE: Browsers may make `cancel` non-cancelable on repeated Escape
// presses without user activation in between, closing the dialog instantly.
drawer.addEventListener('cancel', (event) => {
  if (event.cancelable) {
    event.preventDefault();
    closeDrawer();
  }
});
```

## Implementation for a drawer that also acts as a sidebar

Use this implementation when the same element also becomes a regular, always-visible sidebar under certain conditions (
see [Choose the drawer element](#choose-the-drawer-element)). Toggle `role` from the same media query that switches the
layout (e.g. with `matchMedia()`): remove it while the element acts as a sidebar, and restore `role="dialog"` when it
becomes a drawer again. This guide does not cover the sidebar layout itself.

Follow the [`<dialog>` implementation](#implementation-with-dialog), with these changes:

- **Markup**: `<div class="Drawer" id="drawer" popover="manual" role="dialog" aria-label="Navigation drawer">`.
  `popover="manual"` is REQUIRED; do not use `popover="auto"` or `"hint"`, as their built-in light-dismiss would also
  fire mid-swipe.
- **Open and close**: call `showPopover()` instead of `showModal()` and `hidePopover()` instead of `close()`. The rest
  of the CSS and JS is unchanged.
- **Modality**: a popover is not modal, so the code must do what a modal dialog does natively:
    - Mark the rest of the page `inert` while the drawer is open.
    - Apply `aria-modal="true"` while the drawer is open, and remove it when it closes.
    - Move focus back to the trigger button after the drawer closes.
    - Handle Escape with a `keydown` listener on `document`, since popovers do not fire `cancel`.

```js
const main = document.querySelector('main');

function openDrawer() {
  drawer.showPopover();
  // Mark everything outside the drawer inert immediately on open (include
  // sibling <header>/<footer> landmarks if they live outside <main>).
  main.inert = true;
  drawer.setAttribute('aria-modal', 'true');
  scroller.scrollTo({left: 0, behavior: 'auto'});
}

function onDrawerClosed() {
  // The observer also reports "closed" on page load; ignore it unless open.
  if (!drawer.hasAttribute('aria-modal')) return;
  drawer.hidePopover();
  main.inert = false;
  drawer.removeAttribute('aria-modal');
  openBtn.setAttribute('aria-expanded', 'false');
  openBtn.focus();
}

// Escape key. Listen on document because focus may be inside the
// drawer when the user presses Escape.
document.addEventListener('keydown', (event) => {
  if (event.key === 'Escape') closeDrawer();
});
```

## Fallback strategies

Baseline status for Scroll snap: Widely available. It's been Baseline since 2020-01-15.
Supported by: Chrome 69 (Sep 2018), Edge 79 (Jan 2020), Firefox 68 (Jul 2019), and Safari 11 (Sep 2017).

Baseline status for Intersection observer: Widely available. It's been Baseline since 2019-03-25.
Supported by: Chrome 58 (Apr 2017), Edge 16 (Oct 2017), Firefox 55 (Aug 2017), Safari 12.1 (Mar 2019), and Safari iOS
12.2 (Mar 2019).

The scroll-driven animation that fades the backdrop and `scroll-initial-target` are progressive enhancements with simple
fallbacks that can be easily implemented if wide browser support is required.

### Backdrop fade fallback (no `animation-timeline` support):

Baseline status for Scroll-driven animations: Newly available. It's been Baseline since 2026-10-27.
Supported by: Chrome 115 (Jul 2023), Edge 115 (Jul 2023), Firefox 159 (Oct 2026), and Safari 26 (Sep 2025).

Detect with `CSS.supports('animation-timeline: scroll()')` and write `--drawer-backdrop` from a `scroll` event listener
if not supported. The CSS `@supports` block in step 2 ensures the keyframes never apply in unsupported browsers, so the
JavaScript value is the only writer.

```js
if (!CSS.supports('animation-timeline: scroll()')) {
  scroller.addEventListener('scroll', () => {
    // Same mapping as the @keyframes: 0 scroll = 1 (open),
    // sheet-width scroll = 0 (closed).
    const ratio = 1 - scroller.scrollLeft / sheet.offsetWidth;
    drawer.style.setProperty('--drawer-backdrop', ratio);
  });
}
```

### Initial scroll position fallback (no `scroll-initial-target` support):

Browser support for scroll-initial-target: Limited availability.
Supported by: Chrome 133 (Feb 2025) and Edge 133 (Feb 2025).
Unsupported in: Firefox and Safari.

Detect with `CSS.supports('scroll-initial-target', 'nearest')` and inside `openDrawer()`, jump-scroll the scroller to
the closed position immediately after showing the drawer (`showModal()`, or `showPopover()` when
it [also acts as a sidebar](#implementation-for-a-drawer-that-also-acts-as-a-sidebar)). Without this, the drawer would
appear instantly in the open position with no slide-in animation.

```js
async function openDrawer() {
  drawer.showModal(); // sidebar variant: showPopover(), main.inert = true, and aria-modal="true"

  if (!CSS.supports('scroll-initial-target', 'nearest')) {
    // Jump-scroll to the closed stop so the scroll below
    // animates the drawer in from off-screen.
    scroller.scrollTo({left: scroller.offsetWidth, behavior: 'instant'});
    // Wait two animation frames for the jump-scroll to commit.
    // A single rAF is not enough — the second `scrollTo` would
    // cancel the first before the browser has a chance to apply it.
    await new Promise((r) =>
      requestAnimationFrame(() => requestAnimationFrame(r))
    );
  }

  scroller.scrollTo({left: 0, behavior: 'auto'});
}
```

### `@property` fallback (no registered custom properties):

Baseline status for Registered custom properties: Newly available. It's been Baseline since 2024-07-09.
Supported by: Chrome 85 (Aug 2020), Edge 85 (Aug 2020), Firefox 128 (Jul 2024), and Safari 16.4 (Mar 2023).

`@property` is only needed because the scroll-driven animation interpolates `--drawer-backdrop` between keyframes —
without registration, the property would be treated as a string and would jump between 0 and 1 with no fade. If the
scroll-driven animation fallback above is in place, that JavaScript writes a fresh numeric string to `--drawer-backdrop`
on every scroll frame and never interpolates, so no separate `@property` fallback is needed since all browsers that
support scroll-driven animations also support `@property`.

### Popover API fallback (sidebar variant only):

Baseline status for the api.HTMLElement.showPopover capability: Widely available. It's been Baseline since 2024-04-16.
Supported by: Chrome 114 (May 2023), Edge 114 (Jun 2023), Firefox 125 (Apr 2024), and Safari 17 (Sep 2023).

Baseline status for inert: Widely available. It's been Baseline since 2023-04-11.
Supported by: Chrome 102 (May 2022), Edge 102 (May 2022), Firefox 112 (Apr 2023), and Safari 15.5 (May 2022).

When the drawer [also acts as a sidebar](#implementation-for-a-drawer-that-also-acts-as-a-sidebar), it uses
`popover="manual"` and implements dismissal entirely from JavaScript, so it does not depend on light-dismiss, the
`popovertarget` attribute, or top-layer-managed Escape handling. Aside from top-layer promotion (`showPopover()`) and
`::backdrop`, the only popover behavior it relies on is processing `autofocus` when shown.

If wider browser support is needed, do not branch on feature detection — simply do not use popover at all. Drop the
`popover="manual"` attribute, replace top-layer promotion with `position: fixed` and a high `z-index`, replace
`::backdrop` with a sibling element styled identically (using the same `--drawer-backdrop` custom property), toggle
visibility from a class instead of `showPopover()`/`hidePopover()`, and call `closeBtn.focus({preventScroll: true})` in
`openDrawer()` after making the drawer visible (`preventScroll` avoids scrolling the container early). The rest of the
component (scroll snap, the scroll-driven backdrop animation, the `IntersectionObserver`, and the dismissal handlers) is
unchanged.
